The Almighty is the speaker of this sentence. Did He say it for Himself, or did He say it to teach us to say it? He said it to teach us.

Al-ḥamd (praise) is extolling the one who deserves praise for beautiful attributes. Its opposite is dhamm (blame), which is attributing ugly attributes to one who deserves blame.

You may praise something with which you have no connection, simply because you were pleased by the attributes in it, so in your view it deserves to be praised. For example, you praise the craftsman for a craft he has perfected, even if you have no relation to it.

So praise is sometimes due because the one praised possesses attributes that deserve praise, even if those attributes do not reach you. How much more so when the attributes of praise, glorification and exaltation have effects that reach you? There is no doubt that praise here is more binding.

Therefore we say: every praise, even if directed at a human being, ultimately returns to God Most High, because when you praise a person, you are praising him for an attribute that God bestowed upon him. So praise in its absolute sense, even if addressed to a creature, is praise of God.

The phrase ﴿Praise be to God﴾ (Saba': 1) occurs thirty-eight times in the Qur'an. Of these, it is specifically at the openings of surahs five times: in al-Fatiha, al-An'am, al-Kahf, Saba' and Fatir.

The Almighty began with praise because He began His creation from nothing, so He has the blessing of creating from nothing upon us. Then He supplied us with the means of life, providing the sustenance by which life is preserved, then procreation by which the species is preserved. This is for the material existence of the human being. But the human being is required to have a living activity, and he lives with others, so their movements must support one another and not conflict. Their movements must harmonize, or else creation would perish.

This mutual support cannot be achieved except through a method (manhaj) that defines movements and governs desires; otherwise one would come to build while another comes to demolish. This is in the world. As for the Hereafter, He will prepare us for it with a different preparation, and will return us to something better than what we were in, because we live in this world by means created by God Most High, whereas in the Hereafter we live with the One who causes (al-musabbib), the Holy One, in the very presence of the Real.

In this world we plant, harvest, cook, bake, spin, and so on. These are means that must be practiced. But in the Hereafter you live by His "Be" from the Causer. In this world you fear that bounty will escape you or you will escape it. But in the Hereafter its bliss is lasting, not vanishing or changing. In this world you enjoy according to your capacities, but in the Hereafter you enjoy according to the capacities of your Lord.

So the Almighty brought us into existence from nothing, supplied us from non-existence, and set down for us the method that preserves values and organizes the movement of life before life came into being. Before He created you, He defined for you your purpose, like the craftsman who defines the purpose of his craft before making it. Have you ever seen a craftsman make something and then say: "Look and see what it may be used for"?

Therefore God Most High said:

﴿The Most Merciful. He taught the Qur'an. He created man. He taught him the expression.﴾ (al-Rahman: 1–4)

So the method embodied in the Qur'an was set down first, to define for you your mission and the law of your preservation, before you, O human being, came into being.

Whoever reflects on the verses of praise at the beginnings of the five surahs will find that they cover all these stages. At the beginning of al-An'am:

﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve in their Lord ascribe equals [to Him].﴾ (al-An'am: 1)

Here the Almighty spoke of the beginning of creation. Then He said:

﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (al-An'am: 2). This is the first bringing into existence.

Then at the beginning of al-Kahf He mentions the matter of setting down the method and values:

﴿Praise be to God, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance.﴾ (al-Kahf: 1)

This is the law that governs desires and organizes the movement of life, so that it supports rather than opposes.

At the beginning of Surat Saba', which we are discussing, He mentions praise in the Hereafter: ﴿Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter﴾ (Saba': 1). When you consider praise in the Hereafter, you find it is compound and multiplied, because in this world you praise God for creating the things by which you live through means, whereas in the Hereafter there are no means, only the Causer, the Almighty. So praise in the Hereafter is greater, suited to your living with the Essence of your Lord, glory be to Him.

At the beginning of Fatir:

﴿Praise be to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills.﴾ (Fatir: 1)

We praise God for the values and for the method that the Almighty set down for us through the angels. The angels are the messengers of God to creation. Among them are the guardians (al-ḥafaẓa), among them are those who arrange affairs (al-mudabbirat amran) who manage the affairs of creation, and among them are those whom God commanded to prostrate before you.

Then came Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book), which gathered all of this in:

﴿Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Fatiha: 2). The Lord (al-Rabb) is the Creator who sustains.

﴿The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾ (al-Fatiha: 3–4), that is, in the Hereafter. Then it mentioned the obligation to walk the path of the method:

﴿It is You we worship and You we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked anger or of those who are astray.﴾ (al-Fatiha: 5–7)

Because it gathered the beginning and the end, and this world and the Hereafter, it was named Fatihat al-Kitab (the Opening of the Book), and it was named al-Mathani (the oft-repeated), and it was named Umm al-Qur'an (the Mother of the Qur'an).

So His saying ﴿Praise be to God﴾ (Saba': 1) taught us that we should say it, because people differ in talents, in abilities, in quality of expression, and in the formulation of praise. The eloquent literary man and the illiterate who cannot speak well are not equal in praise and glorification. Therefore God said to us: "Relieve yourselves of this problem. I will teach you a formula in which the eloquent philosopher and the shepherd are equal, and this formula will be the most beloved of formulas of praise to Me. This formula is ﴿Praise be to God﴾ (Saba': 1)."

Thus there came in a hadith the words of our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), in praising his Lord and extolling Him: "Glory be to You; we cannot count the praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself." So when I give a long sermon in praise of God and extolling Him, and you say, "Praise be to God," I do not say that you have fallen short in praising your Lord. It is as if this formula, and its teaching to us, is another blessing deserving of praise, because it equalizes everyone and does not give anyone superiority over anyone in the station of praising God and extolling Him.

When you praise God for having taught you this formula, with what do you praise Him? You praise Him by saying, "Praise be to God." So it is a continuous chain of praise that never ends: praise of God for praise of God. This means that you remain continually praising God, and that God remains continually and forever praised.

As we have said, the differing times on earth and the differing risings and settings were made so that the worship of God would continue without interruption in every particle of time. In every moment there is prayer, in every moment "God is greatest," in every moment "I bear witness that there is no god but God," in every moment "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and so on, so that these words and these acts of worship remain circulating at all times. The entire cosmos is thus absorbed in the remembrance of God and worship of God in a wondrous system. What matters is who receives it well; what matters is the clarity of your receiving apparatus.

As for His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter﴾ (Saba': 1): we have shown that praise in the Hereafter is greater and more magnificent than praise in this world, because in this world you live by means, whereas in the Hereafter you live with the Essence of the Causer, glory be to Him. In this world there is temporary bliss; in the Hereafter there is lasting bliss. In this world there is annihilation; in the Hereafter there is permanence. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said about the Hereafter:

﴿And the last of their call will be: "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (Yunus: 10)

He, glory be to Him, also said, relating of the believers in the Hereafter:

﴿And they will say, "Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the land, to settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of the workers."﴾ (al-Zumar: 74)

And they said:

﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this. We would not have been guided if God had not guided us.﴾ (al-A'raf: 43)

If you ask: what is the basis of praise for the fact that God Most High owns the heavens and the earth? We say: there is a difference between one who serves you in the universe with what you do not own, and one who serves you with what you own. The greatness here is that you benefit here from what you do not own. The heavens and the earth belong to God, and yet they are in your service. The greatness is not in that what you own serves you.

Thus they said to a certain man: "Why do you not buy yourself a car?" He said: "By God, my brothers are many, and all of them have cars, and every day I ride in the car of one of them, and it costs me nothing." So the benefit you derive from what others own is greater than the benefit you derive from what you own yourself. The dominion of God was made for our benefit, and this deserves praise. So O God, do not deprive us of Your blessings.

Another observation: the Almighty wants to reassure the servants. The dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to God alone; had it belonged to another, He would have prevented us from it. So it is as if your Lord says to you: "Be reassured. This is My dominion, and I am your Lord, and I will never abandon you. I have no partner who contends with Me, who would withhold My bounties from you. I am the sole possessor of dominion and sovereignty."

Therefore, when the Almighty says to a thing ﴿Be, and it is﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 47), He said "Be" only because He knows that it cannot fail to be. The proof is His saying about the earth:

﴿And it has listened to its Lord and it has the right to do so﴾ (al-Inshiqaq: 2), that is, it inclined its hearing, and it was right for it to do so. He never said "Be" to a thing except while certain that it would not depart from His command.

Therefore we have previously said that when the Almighty asked us to bear witness that there is no god but Him, He first bore witness to it for Himself, saying:

﴿God bears witness that there is no deity except Him﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 18). This is the testimony of the Essence to the Essence. Therefore He acted in the dominion as one who has no partner. He did not say anything or issue a ruling and then fear that someone would overturn it or amend it.

Then the angels bore witness to it, and then those of knowledge among His servants bore witness to it:

﴿God bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge — standing in justice.﴾ (Ali 'Imran: 18)

So God's testimony is the testimony of the Essence to the Essence; the testimony of the angels is the testimony of the witnessing (mashhad); and the testimony of those of knowledge is the testimony of knowledge and evidence.

We also observe that the Almighty said ﴿to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (Saba': 1). He repeated the relative pronoun "mā" (what), and did not say "to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth," as in His saying glorifying Himself in one place:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God﴾ (al-Jumu'a: 1).

And in another place:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Him﴾ (al-Hashr: 24).

There is a difference between the two expressions, because there is a creation shared between the heavens and the earth, and there is a creation specific to the heavens, and another specific to the earth. If He intends the whole, He says ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ (al-Hashr: 24). If He intends difference, each in its own direction, He says ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ (Saba': 1).

The heavens and the earth are a container (ẓarf) for what is in them of good things, and whoever owns the container and the place owns what is contained in it. So the space here is occupied.

Then the Almighty concludes this verse with ﴿And He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾ (Saba': 1). Al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) is one who places a thing in its proper and suitable position. This is achieved only by one who is expert (khabīr), who knows the thing and knows the position that suits it. Therefore He said, glory be to Him, ﴿And He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾ (Saba': 1), the One who has expertise in the subtleties of things and their inner aspects.

Then He, glory be to Him, wanted to give us a model of this wisdom and this expertise, so He said:

﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it....﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 2:

The meaning of ﴿yaliju﴾ [Saba': 2] is "enters." From it comes the verse ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [Fatir: 13], meaning: He makes each of them enter into the other. So an increase in the night diminishes the day, and an increase in the day diminishes the night; for this reason we see the differences in the times (of prayer and seasons).

But what enters into the earth, within the limits of what our eyes can see? There are things that enter the earth with which we have no direct involvement, such as rainwater, for example, when it descends from the sky: we take from it what we need, and a part of it seeps into the depths of the earth, as God the Exalted says: ﴿So He made it into springs in the earth﴾ [al-Zumar: 21].

And the grain that we sow enters the earth, and from it arises the food that guarantees the continuation of life; this food comes from the multiplication of the grain many times over. Likewise, the dead, whom we entrust to the earth after they die, enter the earth. And you may observe the point of resemblance between the grain you sow and the dead person you bury, in light of His saying: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We return you, and from it We bring you forth once more﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55].

Just as the grain produced seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains, so we ought to extend our mental analogies and say: likewise, when I enter or am buried in the earth after death, I shall come forth to another life more abundant in growth than my life in this world, and more abundant in goodness, beyond what the earth has covered of my faults.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And what descends from the sky﴾ [Saba': 2] — what is it that descends from the sky? Rain descends from it to sustain life, and by water every living thing has life. This concerns the material substance of your existence. As for your spiritual life, angels descend with the values and the method by which souls and hearts live, and the angels who arrange affairs descend with command, those who manage the affairs of creation, and of whom God said: ﴿For him are successive (angels) before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of God﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11].

Some do not understand the meaning of this verse and say: how can the angels guard him from the command of God? They mean that the command of God must be carried out, so how can they guard him from it? The meaning is: they guard him by a guarding that proceeds from the command of God, not as a voluntary act of their own.

The Almighty shows us His power in the sending down of rain when we carry out the process of distilling water in laboratories and pharmacies. Consider how much a cup of distilled water costs, and how much time and effort it takes. But as for the rain, the power of God distils it for you without your feeling it. The heat of the sun evaporates the water that forms the clouds; then the winds drive it to wherever God wills for it to fall. And among His wisdom, exalted is He, is that He made three-quarters of the globe water, so that the area of evaporation would be vast, and thus the rain suffices the needs of living beings.

We illustrate this phenomenon with a cup of water that you leave for a month: it decreases by only a few centimetres. But if you pour it onto the floor of the room, it dries before you leave it. Why? Because you have widened the area from which the water evaporates.

Rainwater is the sweet, pure water from which humans, animals and birds drink, and with which we irrigate crops and the surfaces of the land. What remains, God channels into the depths of the earth until it is needed. Thus rain is one of the signs of God that point to His power, exalted is He.

Then He says, glorified is He: ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ [Saba': 2] — that is, what rises up. The Qur'an has indicated this matter in His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10], that is, the effects of the methodical obligation ascend to God, exalted is He.

But note, in the phrasing of ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ [Saba': 2], the use of the preposition (fi, "in") and not "ila" (to): ﴿ya'ruju ilayha﴾ would be the expected form. We know that a particle has a meaning in itself, but this meaning needs something to be joined to it so as to give an understood sense. The particle (fi) indicates containment, as when you say: water in the cup. But if you say (fi) on its own, it indicates nothing.

When scholars encountered many constructions in which they found particles that they thought were superfluous, or that carried the meaning of another particle, they said, regarding ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ [Saba': 2], that (fi) here means (ila, "to"). But why did the phrasing shift from (ila) to (fi)? Then it must be that it carries the sense of containment.

To clarify, we may cite what we have said about His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71]. Some said it means "upon the trunks of palm trees," but this is an imprecise understanding of God's speech, because (fi) here gives me both meanings: the meaning of (ala, "upon") and the meaning of (fi, "in").

Crucifixion is the fixing of one thing upon another, and this meaning is conveyed by (ala), but it is deficient. If you intended (ala) alone, you would have to say: "I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees with a strong crucifixion, such that the parts of the crucified enter into the thing upon which he is crucified." Thus the complete meaning of crucifixion is conveyed only by (fi).

Take a matchstick and place it on your hand or on your finger, and wind a light thread around it. In this case the thread alone holds the matchstick in place. But if you tighten the thread strongly around it, the matchstick enters the skin until it almost disappears within it. This is the crucifixion intended: that you fix the crucified onto that on which he is crucified with force, by nails or ropes or the like.

For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71] and did not say "upon the trunks of palm trees," because (fi) conveys the meanings of both elevation and containment together.

Likewise in ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ [Saba': 2], and He did not say "what ascends to it," because (ila) does not convey the required meaning, for (ila) indicates the goal. As you say: I travelled from Cairo to Alexandria. Heaven is not the ultimate goal of the ascent of the good word; rather its goal and final end is God, mighty and majestic. The heaven is only a path that leads to the highest end, and we have already said that heaven is everything that is above you.

This particular meaning of the preposition is also evident in His saying: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], where (ila) is used because forgiveness is the goal that the believer seeks and hastens toward.

And He said: ﴿Those hasten in the good deeds﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 61].

He did not say "to the good deeds," because the good deeds are not the goal; rather they are stations in which the believer ascends and rises, and whenever he reaches a good deed he looks towards a better one. So the good deeds are like a space in which he travels, not a destination to which he goes.

Likewise, when the Almighty spoke of those who denied the messengers, He said: ﴿So they put their hands into their mouths﴾ [Ibrahim: 9].

Some say: that is, "to their mouths." But no: (fi) carries the sense of exaggeration in rejecting the method that the messengers brought. The meaning is that when the messengers brought the method, the deniers did not accept it and said to them: "Keep your words to yourselves," meaning: it will avail us nothing. They put their hands inside their mouths and bit on them out of rage at what they heard from the messengers. This meaning is not conveyed by the phrase "to their mouths."

Then He, glorified is He: ﴿And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving﴾ [Saba': 2]. The attribute "Merciful" (al-Rahim) means the One who prevents harm from befalling in the first place, as He said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra': 82].

The word ﴿healing﴾ [al-Isra': 82] means: a sickness has befallen you that arose from heedlessness, and the Qur'an came to remind you, alert you, and heal your soul from this heedlessness. If heedlessness does not exist, the Qur'an is a mercy that prevents the disease from occurring at the outset. (Rahim) is an intensive form derived from mercy (rahma).

Likewise, ﴿al-Ghafur﴾ [Saba': 2] is an intensive form derived from forgiveness (maghfira). The Almighty frequently emphasises this attribute, because He created man, and knows that he will not always walk the straight path, and will inevitably at some point deviate from the upright method. For this reason He said: ﴿He makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and pardons much﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 15].

We have said that were it not for the attributes of mercy, repentance and forgiveness, the sinner would persist in his sins and despair of returning to the straight path, and this is what we called (faqid, the one who has lost hope), and by it the whole society suffers. But if he knows that he has a Lord who forgives sins and accepts repentance, he turns to it and repents. And why would he not, since God has guaranteed him the forgiveness of his sins if he repents and turns back?

Thus God legislated repentance to show mercy to creation, to show mercy to all creatures, and to bestow a kindness upon them. When He turns in forgiveness to the sinner, He protects society from his evil, and He protects him from the consequences of his sins. For this reason He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118], that is, He legislated repentance to open for them the scope to turn back and a path of return to God, so that there is no ferocity and persistence in evil, and the sinner does not become a tyrant.

When we reflect on His saying: ﴿And if you should count God's favour, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34], we find that the beginning of the verse occurs in the same wording in two places, but the ending differs. In one verse: ﴿And if you should count God's favour, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34], and in the other: ﴿And if you should count God's favour, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 18].

When some stopped at this verse they objected, saying: how can a favour be counted when it is one? ﴿And if you should count God's favour, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. The answer: the favour that appears to you as one in its outward aspect contains within it many favours. This became clear to us after the sciences advanced and the science of the elements of things appeared. The apple, for example, appears to you as one favour in its outward form, but the science of elements shows us that within it are many favours, and various elements and benefits. It is a favour containing favours.

A favour implies: a favour, a benefactor, and one who is benefited. The favour in itself is so numerous that it cannot be counted or enumerated. For this reason He used the particle (in, "if"), which indicates doubt, and did not say, for example, "if you count God's favours," because this is a field in which no one can hope to succeed, and God's favours are not liable to enumeration.

Therefore no one has ventured to attempt to count God's favours, even after universities and specialised colleges of statistics were established, which tried to count everything except this matter, because the undertaking of counting and enumeration implies the possibility of reaching the enumeration of what is counted.

As for the one who receives the favour, who is man, he is a wrongdoer and ungrateful: a wrongdoer to himself and to others, and ungrateful for the favour. Were we to hold him to account for this, we would deprive him of this favour; but what has protected him from this deprivation is that the One who bestows the favour is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful. This is so when we look at the Benefactor, glorified is He.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you..."﴾.

Here again He speaks to us about the Hour. At the end of Surat al-Ahzab He says: "The people ask you about the Hour" [al-Ahzab: 63], whereas here they deny it: "Those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come upon us.'" [Saba': 3] That is, the Resurrection.

So why do they deny it? Yes, they deny it, because they have been excessive against their own souls and have persisted in their error, and the Resurrection will not be in their favour. Therefore they flee from it through denial and rejection. Even the brethren of these deniers, those who love to find fault with the words of God, say: "If God has decreed everything for the servant, decreeing obedience and decreeing disobedience, then why does He punish him for disobedience?"

And it is noticeable that none of them, in return, has said: "Then why does He reward him for obedience?" This indicates that this stance is mistaken and illogical, and that they fear punishment. The one who utters this saying only says it because he is confident of the abundance of his evil deeds, and it is in his interest to deny the Resurrection and reject it, like the one who said: "And I do not think the Hour will ever occur; and even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination." [al-Kahf: 36]

So their frequent questioning about the Hour and their denial of it indicate their fear of it. Rather, they are terrified merely at the thought of affirming it, because they know well that if they hide from people, they will not hide from God, and if they conceal matters from the judgement of the earth, they will not conceal them from the judgement of heaven. Neither argument nor eloquence of speech nor the falsification of facts will benefit them on the Day of Resurrection.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am only a human being like you, and you bring your disputes before me, and perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I decide in his favour. Whoever I decide in his favour concerning the right of his brother, let him not take it, for I have only cut off for him a piece of the Fire."

The judge rules by argument and by evidence, and a speaker may mislead the judge and take the rights of others unjustly, as some lawyers do now. This is in this world; but in the Hereafter you are in a court whose judge is the Truth, glory be to Him.

So: these people deny the Resurrection because it is the riddle that perplexes them, the truth that disturbs their sleep and terrifies them, the truth that shakes their standing and ends their dominion. Even if they feel secure in this world because of their status and control, in the Resurrection they will come as He said: "And you have indeed come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you behind your backs." [al-An'am: 94]...

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, responds to their denial of the Hour, saying, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): "Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you...'" That is: say with full mouth, "Yes" (bala). "Bala" is a negation of the preceding negation in their saying "The Hour will not come upon us." When we nullify a negation, we affirm its opposite; so the meaning of "bala" is: it will indeed come.

Then the discourse does not stop at that, but emphasises this matter with an oath: "Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you...'" So the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches His Messenger to swear by His Essence, while being certain that it will come to them, and the Truth, glory be to Him, does not teach His Messenger a false oath. The Truth, glory be to Him, is truthful without swearing, so what of when He swears to you?

His saying after it, "the Knower of the unseen...", contains an indication that we do not report the Hour nor swear to its coming out of nothing, but on the basis of what we have of knowledge of the unseen. It is therefore certainly coming. Not only that, but He will confront you with a complete reckoning of sins, the great and the small, the apparent and the hidden, for the Knower of the unseen nothing escapes, however well concealed it is, and however skilled you are at hiding it from people.

"The Knower of the unseen, from whom not an atom's weight escapes [Him] in the heavens or on the earth, nor is anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register." [Saba': 3] "Yaʿzub" (escape): does not go absent from His knowledge.

In many verses the Truth, glory be to Him, uses the atom (dharrah) as an example of the smallness of things; it is the mote seen in the sunlight and not seen in the shade because of its tiny size...

Consider the precision of expression here: He mentions only the atom, the smallest thing man has known, then mentions what is smaller than it and the smallest, so that however far we progress in splitting the atom, we find in the Word of God a reserve for what we will reach...

One may ask: if the Truth, glory be to Him, favours us by making us aware of the atom and what is fine among things, what is the distinction in His knowing the greater of them?

It is said: this is a subtle point of the Qur'anic style. A thing may be hidden from you either because it is extremely small, so that your instruments cannot perceive it, or because it is great, so that your perception cannot reach it; it is too great for you to encompass. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, has dominion over the smallest thing and the greatest thing: nothing small escapes Him for its smallness, nor anything great for its greatness.

The Truth, glory be to Him, does not merely have His knowledge encompass what is in His creation, but He also records it in a miraculous, enduring Book. There is a difference between informing of knowledge by statement and recording it. If the knowledge is not recorded, you may say whatever you wish; but once it is recorded, it becomes a proof against you.

Therefore, when the Truth, glory be to Him, gives us a matter in the universe, He preserves it along with the Qur'an, whereas you only preserve what is to your benefit. And as long as the Truth, glory be to Him, preserves it, this means it is an event that will certainly occur; otherwise He would not have recorded and preserved it. He, glory be to Him, knows perfectly that nothing occurs in His dominion except what He has known. So: He wrote because He knew, not knew because it was written. And who commanded its writing? His knowledge, glory be to Him. So knowledge is prior.

But why, when they asked about the Hour or denied it, did God remind them of His knowledge of every small and great thing, saying: "from whom not an atom's weight escapes [Him] in the heavens or on the earth, nor is anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register"?

It is said: the Truth, glory be to Him, mentioned to them the all-encompassing nature of His knowledge in order to divert them from thinking about the matter of the Hour, and to occupy them with their sins, which are reckoned against them, and nothing of them escapes God. Then they will say, "Would that we had not asked," as He said:

"O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made apparent to you, would distress you..." [al-Ma'idah: 101].

So: they asked about the Hour, and He took them to another arena that unsettles and shakes them whenever they know that the knowledge of God, exalted is He, encompasses everything in the heavens and on the earth...

"That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds..."

It is strange that the provision itself should be described as noble (karīm). Nobility (karam) is an attribute of the Provider who bestows the provision upon you. So what of it, if the provision itself is noble, going out to you and knowing your place...

﴿سَعَوْا فِيٓ آيَاتِنَا﴾: ... حرّضوا الناس عليها ليزهد فيها من كان مُقبلاً عليها، ويخرج منها من كان فيها ويتملّص منها. سعَوْا في آيات الله، وهي القرآن، ليُبطلوه ويصرفوا الناس عنه. ولماذا؟ لأنهم واثقون من أثر القرآن في القلوب، فلو أعطاه الناس آذانهم لابدّ أن يؤثر فيهم ويجذبهم إلى ساحة الإيمان، فتنفعل به قلوبهم، وتلهج به ألسنتهم.

وهؤلاء هم الذين قالوا: ﴿لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ﴾ [فصلت: 26]. ولو كان القرآن كلاماً عادياً لا أثر له، لَمَا نَهَوْا عن سماعه، ولا شوّشوا عليه، ولا خافوا من سماعه.

﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾: من "عاجَزَ"، أي حاول كلٌّ من الطرفين إثبات عجز الآخر. تقول: "عاجزني"، أي جعلني أفعل فعلاً أعجز عنه. فكأنهم يريدون بسعيهم في آيات الله أن يُثبتوا عجزها، وأن يُعجزوا الدعوة عن أن تبلغ مداها، ويُعجزوا رسولَ الله عن أن يتمّم رسالته، ويُعجزوا منهجَ الله عن أن يصل إلى خلق الله.

لكن، يُعاجزون مَن؟ أيُعاجزون الله؟ كيف، وهو سبحانه الذي أرسل الرسل، وتكفّل بنصرتهم وعدم التخلّي عنهم، وما كانت الحروب والقتال بين الرسل والمكذِّبين إلا سبباً يأتي من خلاله نصرُ الله، كما قال سبحانه: ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [التوبة: 14].

وقال سبحانه: ﴿وَلَقَدْ سَبَقَتْ كَلِمَتُنَا لِعِبَادِنَا الْمُرْسَلِينَ * إِنَّهُمْ لَهُمُ الْمَنْصُورُونَ * وَإِنَّ جُنْدَنَا لَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ [الصافات: 171-172].

إذن: مَن سيُعاجزون؟ ربما يُقبل أن يُعاجزوا رسولَ الله ﷺ أو يُعاجزوا المؤمنين، أما الحق سبحانه فهو الغالب القادر، فهل يستطيع أحد أن يُعجز الله ويتغلب عليه سبحانه، فيجعله عاجزاً، وهو سبحانه القادر الغالب؟

فمعنى ﴿سَعَوْا فِيٓ آيَاتِنَا﴾ أي: وضعوا المكايد والعراقيل في طريقها ليُفسدوا أمر الدعوة، وحتى يردّوها على رسول الله ﷺ في فمه الذي قالها. ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾ حالة كونهم معاجزين، يعني: يسيرون مع خالقهم في مضمار واحد؛ الله يريد أن يُعجزهم، وهم يريدون أن يُعجزوا الله، وأن يكونوا في مكان القدرة الإلهية العليا، ليُثبتوا أن الدعوة باطلة.

ثم يُبيّن سبحانه جزاء هؤلاء المعاجزين: ﴿أُولَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ﴾ [سبأ: 5]. و"الرِّجْز" و"الرُّجْز" (أي العذاب المُهلِك، وأصله في اللغة: الحِمل الثقيل)، وأصله الذنب، وما يترتب عليه من عقوبة...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 34, verse 6:

Here is a reassurance for our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is as though his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is saying to him: "O Muhammad, do not despair of those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, and do not be troubled. The One who made some of the disbelievers those who strive for corruption and try to frustrate their Creator has also made for you those who support your call and strengthen you from among the believers in the signs of Allah, who know that they are the truth and that what these people say is nonsense, which is falsehood."

Just as He attributed to them striving in falsehood and frustration, He attributed to the believers knowledge of the signs of Allah, affirmation of them, and acknowledgment that they are the truth. He reassured the Messenger of Allah that these people will not corrupt your affair for you, nor will they extinguish the light of Allah, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [al-Saff: 8].

And He said: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33].

So the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾ mean: they bear witness on your behalf that you are upon the truth, and that you have brought them a method that is the truth and guides to a straight path. Therefore: set these people opposite those who strove against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, and draw a comparison between these and those.

The disbelievers who strove in corruption against Our signs are stripped of the support of power; rather, power is against them and lies in wait for them. As for those who were given knowledge and bore witness to the Messenger of Allah, they are supporters of the divine power, and power is with them, supporting them. So which of the two scales is heavier?

And the meaning of ﴿And those who have been given knowledge﴾ [Saba: 6] is: those among the believers in Muhammad (ﷺ) who were given knowledge, who affirmed him and affirmed his miracle and his message. Or: those among the People of the Book who were given knowledge, the Jews or the Christians, for the fair-minded among them know the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah and recognise him as they recognise their own sons. These are the ones who went to Yathrib before the Messenger of Allah's mission, awaiting his coming, and they used to seek victory through him over those who disbelieved, saying: "The time of a new prophet has drawn near; we will follow him and slay you with him, the slaying of 'Ad and Iram."

﴿But when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89].

Therefore the Qur'an, in its argument against the disbelievers, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "You are not a messenger." Say:﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43], meaning: in reply to them,

﴿"Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43], meaning: Allah, who sent me with the miracle,

﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43], meaning: among the Jews and the Christians, the people of the Torah and the Gospel.

And knowledge ('ilm): it is every proposition that is held with certainty, which corresponds to reality and for which there is evidence. Anything other than that is not considered knowledge. If a proposition is not held with certainty, it does not enter into knowledge; it is rather in doubt, or in conjecture, or in illusion. If a proposition is held with certainty but has no reality corresponding to it, this is ignorance (jahl).

Therefore we have previously said: the ignorant person is not the one who does not know; rather, the ignorant person is the one who knows a proposition that contradicts reality. As for the one who does not know, he is the unlettered person whose mind is completely empty; therefore he accepts what you say, unlike the ignorant person, for whom you must first prove the error of his proposition, and then persuade him of what you want.

If a proposition is held with certainty and has a reality corresponding to it, but you cannot demonstrate it, then it is imitation (taqlid)...

Knowledge, though it has many kinds, can be confined to two: religious knowledge and cosmic knowledge. Religious knowledge, or the knowledge of the Law (ʿilm al-sharʿ), has its source in heaven; it is conveyed by a messenger with a miracle, and no one has any role in it. Humans have, in knowledge of the Law, only transmission, narration and conveyance from the Messenger. This knowledge is what defines for us the lawful and the unlawful. The knowledge of the Law did not come to interfere with cosmic knowledge; it came to regulate the differing desires. For this reason people differ regarding this knowledge.

As for cosmic knowledge, it is the knowledge that investigates all kinds of existence: in minerals, in plants, in animals, and in humans. This knowledge rests on the activity of the intellect, and people do not differ about it, because it is material, relying on research, experiment and observation. For this reason people compete in it, and sometimes some of them steal it from others.

Through this cosmic knowledge a human raises the level of his life. The Creator, Mighty and Majestic, has given you all the constituents and necessities of life, and if you wish for the comfort of life, you must employ your mind and thought on the provisions of the universe around you, so that you discover the secrets and signs of Allah the Exalted in His cosmos, through which you elevate your life...

So the meaning of ﴿And those who have been given knowledge﴾ is: the knowledge of the Law, namely those who believed in you and affirmed you by the miracle, that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that what you brought is the truth ﴿that has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾...

Likewise, those who were given cosmic knowledge have a role in affirming the messengers and supporting them with the cosmic knowledge they have been given, which points to Allah. If the Qur'an is the written Book of Allah, then the universe with its various kinds is the witnessed, visible Book of Allah.

And recite, if you wish, the words of the True, Glorified and Exalted:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it fruits of diverse colours﴾ [Fatir: 27], this is plants;

﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of diverse colours, and deep black﴾ [Fatir: 27], and this is minerals;

﴿And among people﴾ [Fatir: 28], humankind;

﴿and beasts and cattle﴾ [Fatir: 28], meaning: animals;

﴿of diverse colours likewise﴾ [Fatir: 28].

Then the True, glory be to Him, concludes with His words:

﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir: 28]. Which scholars? The scholars of the universe, who investigate its diverse kinds, its scientific, social and health laws, and so on.

These scholars fear Allah, because they witness His secrets in His cosmos and make people aware of them. They are soldiers of the call: if they believe, they affirm the power of Allah. Indeed, the scholars of the Law cite their words, and they manifest the power of Allah in the universe through their scientific theories. Thus cosmic knowledge has a great mission in the field of calling to Allah.

But who among these — the scholars of the Law or the scholars of the universe — sees that what Muhammad brought is the truth?

If we say the scholars of the Law, they have borne witness to the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him, whether among the believers in his message or among the scholars of the People of the Book. And if we say the scholars of the universe, they too have borne witness to the Messenger of Allah and supported him with what they possess of the secrets of Allah's power...

So the words of the Exalted, ﴿And those who have been given knowledge﴾, mean: the knowledge of the Law sent down from above, or the cosmic knowledge based on research and observation. And His words ﴿who have been given knowledge﴾ — whether it is religious knowledge or cosmic knowledge — show that knowledge is a giving (ītāʾ); there is no scholar by himself; rather, knowledge is a giving from Allah, even in the knowledge of the cosmos. For this reason He did not say "they knew," but ﴿have been given knowledge﴾...

We note in the style of the verse that the second object of the verb (yara, "see") came in the form of the independent pronoun: ﴿those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, and He did not say only "the truth" but "huwa al-haqq" (it is the truth). This independent pronoun means that other than it is not truth; the truth is what was revealed to a messenger, and whatever else is not truth, as if this is a quality given to none but him (ﷺ).

Similar to it is His saying, related from our master Abraham:

﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 78]. He did not say "Who created me guides me," because that could allow that someone else guides you; rather, ﴿fa-huwa yahdeeni﴾ restricts guidance to Him, glory be to Him and exalted...

So His saying "huwa al-haqq" indicates that the truth is one: it is what Allah has sent down, and whatever else is false...

The truth is: the established thing that does not change and cannot be denied. And how can you deny the truth, when you, wanting to support yourself in something, say: "This is my right," meaning it belongs to me and no one disputes it with me; the claim you make is that this is your right.

And the truth, besides being a fixed matter, benefits you. It therefore has two features or proofs: the first is that it is the established truth and what is other than it is false; the second is that its benefit returns to you. For this reason He said after it: ﴿and guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. So if you do not accept the truth for its own sake and are zealous for it, then accept it for the benefit that returns to you. These two matters are the grounds for adhering to the truth.

The meaning of "al-ʿAziz" (the Mighty) is the One who cannot be overcome or subdued. From it comes our saying: "ʿazza ʿalayya kadha" (it was difficult for me), meaning I was unable to do it; and "fulan ʿazīz" (so-and-so is mighty), meaning no one can subdue him. The quality of might is a quality of intimidation: when you turn away from this truth, know that you are disobeying One who is Mighty, who cannot be subdued, who overcomes and is not overcome.

Then He, glory be to Him, follows it with a quality of encouragement: "al-Hamid" (the Praiseworthy), meaning the one praised for the blessings He bestows, which encourages you to seek more of Allah's blessings.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 7:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say...﴾ [Saba: 7]. It is known that speech requires a speaker and one to whom it is addressed. The speakers are those who disbelieved. They said: to whom? They said to one another while they conversed together, or the leader among them said to his follower who imitates him. As for their words, they are ﴿Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are completely disintegrated, that you will indeed be in a new creation?﴾ [Saba: 7].

What draws our attention in this statement is that they described the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the word "man" (rajul), which is indefinite, intending by it mockery, disdain, and belittling of his status (ﷺ).

This in itself shows their foolishness and dullness of mind, for they are the very ones who described him as the Messenger of Allah when they said, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7]. This shows their foolishness.

They are also the ones who said, when revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." This is strange of them, for in times of trial and adversity they acknowledge that Muhammad has a Lord.

Their words ﴿will inform you﴾ [Saba: 7] derive from naba' (news), which is applied only to important news, not to news in general. For example, when I say to you: "Today I ate such and such, and went to such and such a place," this is not considered a naba', because it is ordinary information. But naba' is extraordinary, important, and great information, as the words of Allah the Exalted show: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ [al-Naba': 1-2].

The meaning of ﴿when you are completely disintegrated﴾ [Saba: 7]: tamzeeq (disintegration) is the nullification of the whole from its parts and the separation of the parts from one another. For example, I am now sitting on a chair. This chair is a whole composed of parts: wood, nails, glue, cotton, fabric, and so on. The disintegration of this whole is that I separate these parts from one another, and so this whole collapses into parts.

Here we must distinguish between kull (the whole) and kulli (the universal). The kull is composed of many things, yet they differ in reality: the wood is not the nail, the nail is not the glue, the glue is not the fabric; each part has its own composition.

As for the kulli, it applies to many separate things that are nonetheless identical in reality. For example, we say: "human" with respect to individuals is a kulli, because "human" applies to the whole collection, such that one says of each individual: "human." But regarding the whole, I do not say the wood is a chair.

This is tamzeeq. So what did ﴿completely disintegrated﴾ [Saba: 7] add?

That is: a severe disintegration that disintegrates the whole and disintegrates the part. Thus disintegration has stages and forms. The meaning of ﴿you are completely disintegrated﴾ [Saba: 7] is the exhaustive reaching of the smallest thing the disintegrated body can reach. We observe this disintegration in the decomposition of the dead, the dissolution of his parts and elements, until they go into the earth and no trace of them remains.

From this is their saying: ﴿And they say: "When we have gone astray in the earth, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 10].

The meaning of ﴿gone astray in the earth﴾ [al-Sajdah: 10] is: we went into it and were lost in its wilderness.

Disintegration has many causes. Whoever dies and is buried, the earth disintegrates him; whoever dies burned, the fire disintegrates him; the winds may scatter him and his particles disperse; and whoever is eaten by animals and birds, and so on.

Despite this disintegration, scattering, and dispersal, the power of Allah is able to restore the human being anew. Read: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an. Rather, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing. When we have died and become dust, that is a distant return."﴾ [Qaf: 1-3]. They deem resurrection far-fetched, so the Qur'an responds to them: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them...﴾ [Qaf: 4], meaning: do not be astonished, for every particle that has been scattered, We know it, know its place, and are able to restore it. ﴿And with Us is a preserved record﴾ [Qaf: 4], meaning: it is not mere knowledge, but recorded, preserved knowledge, which is not subject to change or alteration.

As for his words: ﴿Indeed, you are in a new creation﴾ [Saba: 7], the new creation is that a thing is returned to its original composition, like one who turns a suit inside out, for example, so that it becomes new. Why? Because he has re-formed it anew.

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says:

﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there in him madness...﴾.

This statement, like the one before it, requires a speaker and one addressed. Its speaker may be the first speaker who said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you..." (Saba': 7), or it may be the other party who heard the first speaker and replied: "Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?" (Saba': 8).

The meaning of "Has he invented..." (Saba': 8) derives from iftira' (fabrication), which is the deliberate telling of a lie. "Or is there madness in him..." (Saba': 8): that is, jinnah (madness), meaning that his speech is nonsense, without weight, and cannot be called either true or false. But why did they accuse the Messenger of Allah of being possessed by madness after they had accused him of lying and fabrication?

They say: because this accusation is itself a lie, and the liar always fears that his condition will be exposed and his lie uncovered. Therefore he tries to create an escape route for himself when his lie is proven. So they said: "Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?" (Saba': 8). Thus, when the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah is established, and it becomes clear that he is neither a liar nor a fabricator, the accuser finds a way out and says: "By Allah, I do not know whether he is a fabricator or whether there is madness in him." And since his truthfulness has been established, then there is madness in him.

It is strange that the disbelievers of Makkah should describe the Messenger of Allah as a liar and a fabricator against Allah, when he is one of them. They knew of him only that he was the truthful and trustworthy (al-Sadiq al-Amin), and they had never found him to lie at all. They never saw him as an orator or a poet, although they were people of eloquence and champions of the word, and the appreciation of language and the understanding of Arabic styles were not hidden from them. It was therefore incumbent upon them to think first before directing this accusation at the Messenger of Allah.

Moreover, does eloquence come later? Does genius come after the age of forty? It is well known that genius appears in the late second decade or early third decade of life, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained among them forty years before he conveyed to them a single word from Allah.

Therefore the Qur'an addresses them and argues with them by proof, saying on the tongue of our master, the Messenger of Allah: "I had dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then use your reason?" (Yunus: 16). That is: consider the matter and understand it, for you are the people of eloquence and of the eloquent tongue, and among you are the orators and poets who filled the world with speech. Have you seen anything of this in me?

So, the one who said: "Or is there madness in him..." (Saba': 8) hedged his bets for himself: when the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah appears, he says: "I said that he is either a liar or a madman."

Then the Truth refutes these people: "Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and in far-off error" (Saba': 8). The word "Bal" (rather) indicates the turning away from what precedes it, its negation and rejection, then the affirmation of what follows it. It negates that the Messenger of Allah is a fabricator and negates that he is a madman, because you never experienced lying from him before, and you never saw in him any sign of madness, since a madman is not praised for an act nor blamed for an act, and he is not described as truthful or lying. You had already praised the Messenger of Allah and said of him, "the truthful and trustworthy."

Therefore Allah, the Truth, Glorified is He, says: "Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character" (al-Qalam: 1-4). And can a madman be described as having a great moral character? Can a madman be described with good manners, faithfulness, or other qualities of praiseworthy character?

So how do you describe the Messenger of Allah as a madman, when you have testified to him the chief of praiseworthy qualities of the human soul, which is trustworthiness, and you used to entrust him with your possessions and place them with him? Therefore the Messenger of Allah left Imam Ali behind him after he emigrated, to return the deposits and trusts to their owners.

After Allah, the Truth, Glorified is He, had nullified their lie against the Messenger of Allah, He establishes what they deserve for it of punishment: "Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and in far-off error" (Saba': 8). They are in punishment because they accused the Messenger of Allah of lying and fabrication against Allah, while the Messenger of Allah did not lie and did not fabricate against Allah. And they are in far-off error because they described the Messenger of Allah as a madman, which is a thing that corrupts his constitution; but he did not lie. So: the punishment corresponds to the accusation of fabrication against Allah, and far-off error corresponds to their accusation of him (ﷺ) of madness.

Then Allah, the Truth, Glorified is He, says:

"Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth...?"

Interrogative here. The meaning: how can they say this and neglect the signs of Allah in His creation, which are plain to them and not hidden from them? They live in the desert, where the sky is open to them. It has no buildings that block the signs of Allah from them, as city dwellers have. They rarely see the sun or the moon, and when an eclipse occurs they learn of it only from newspaper reports.

As for the people of the desert, they live in a vast wilderness, and the face of the sky is visible to them. The sun is their companion by day, and the moon and stars by night. They look at these signs and contemplate them. Therefore the Arab man, while contemplating the universe around him and while in his natural disposition (fitrah), said: "A sky with constellations, an earth with mountain paths, and seas with waves. A footprint indicates the walker, and a dropping indicates the camel. Does this not indicate the existence of the All-Subtle, the All-Aware?"

So then: how can you accuse the Messenger of Allah while the signs of the Truth are clear before you, and neglect the signs of Allah? ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth?﴾ The meaning of ﴿what is before them﴾ (مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ) is in front of them, and ﴿what is behind them﴾ (وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ) is behind them. You may add their right and left, because wherever you go in these directions you will find nothing but sky. Even if you said "beneath them" and tried to pierce the earth, you would eventually reach a sky on the other side. However, He did not say "beneath them," because a person cannot pierce the earth to its end.

Then, what greatness there is in the creation of the sky with this expanse, and yet without pillars! You cannot set up a tent several meters wide except by fastening it with ropes and stakes and raising it with poles. If the wind blew upon it, it would uproot its stakes and poles and collapse on those inside. So how do you pass by the signs of Allah in the sky and the earth without contemplating them?

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them﴾ as He caused it to swallow Qarun, ﴿or We shall make pieces of the sky fall upon them﴾ as the thunderbolt descended previously upon the deniers of the messengers. (كِسَفاً) is the plural of (كِسْفَة), meaning a piece. ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back (to Allah)﴾: a sign means a lesson and an admonition for every servant who seeks to return to his Lord.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, placed these signs in His creation so that they would remind every heedless person, turn back every disbeliever, and incline him to return to his Lord. Had the disbeliever returned to his Lord, He would have accepted him.

So then: Allah, the Truth, created the creatures and wills to make them happy. But we must test who deserves happiness, and distinguish between those who obey the method of Allah and those who disobey it.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, opens for His servants, even the disbelievers among them, the door of hope so that they may return to His presence. It has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said:

He opened, through repentance and turning back (to Allah), the door of return to Him. This is especially so when the means that call a person to repentance are complete for him, such as advancing age or illness, etc., which keep a person away from the places of desires and call him to turn towards Allah and set right what has corrupted his relationship with his Lord and Creator. Then, if he returns to Him on the Day of Resurrection, he returns purified of his sins. That is because the creation is His creation and His handiwork, and the maker wills good and happiness for his handiwork.

We have previously mentioned the hadith that explains that the heavens, the earth, the mountains and the seas rebelled against the son of Adam and asked their Lord, blessed and exalted, for permission to destroy him. The sky said: "O Lord, permit me to fall in pieces upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your bounty and withheld gratitude to You, etc." So what did the Truth, glory be to Him, say to it? He said: "Leave them and what I have created. Had you created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, I am their physician."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us: "O mountains, repeat praise with him, and the birds..."﴾

Having opened the door of repentance to His servants, and given them hope even the disbelievers among them, and after they had done to the Messenger of Allah what they had done and had striven against the signs of Allah to frustrate them, Allah, glory be to Him, is still merciful to them and eager for them, so He draws their attention to the vastness of His mercy.

It is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying to them: Do not magnify your deeds and your sins before the mercy of Allah, and let these sins not prevent you from repentance and returning to Allah, even if you have sinned. Among the Messengers there were those in whom a lapse occurred, although they were prophets. So Allah, in all this, is seeking to find an excuse for them.

Therefore after this He mentions the account of our master Dawud (Dawud, peace be upon him): ﴿And indeed We gave David bounty from Us﴾ . . . In another place He clarified what happened to our master Dawud:

﴿And David thought that We had tried him, so he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24].

So: do not be ashamed to turn back to Allah. For your master, to whom I gave such-and-such, when a lapse occurred from him, sought forgiveness, fell down bowing and turned in repentance. He, glory be to Him, wants to soften their hearts so that they return to the embrace of their Lord.

Likewise our master Sulayman (Sulayman, peace be upon him): a lapse occurred from him, so Allah tried him and punished him, and he repented and sought forgiveness. Recite:

﴿And We did test Sulayman and We placed upon his throne a body...﴾ [Sad: 34]. And "body" (jasad) means that he became unable to move by himself.

﴿Then he turned in repentance. He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me; indeed You are the Bestower﴾ [Sad: 34-35]. So what became of his affair after he sought forgiveness?

﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running by his command gently wherever he directed. And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound in chains﴾ [Sad: 36-38].

The word (fadl) (bounty) means the surplus thing. Allah gave Dawud, peace be upon him, many blessings that He did not give to many of the prophets: He gave him chosen status, He gave him the method (manhaj), and He increased him in another blessing specific to him, namely that He made iron soft for him, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We made iron soft for him, [saying]: Make coats of mail...﴾

And the word "minna" (from Us) indicates that the blessing is not from your essence but from Allah, so placing the prepositional phrase first here conveys the restriction of the blessing to the Bestower, glory be to Him.

Bounty from Allah comes to all people, but the Messengers have distinguished blessings and a greater bounty in the form of miracles. Allah, glory be to Him, shows His bounty upon His Prophet Dawud by His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo [the praises] with him, and the birds; and We made iron soft for him.﴾

"O mountains" is a call; Allah calls the mountains because they hear and comprehend this call. "Awwibi" (echo) means: repeat after him what he says and what he recites of the Zabur or of the remembrance. Here is evidence that he understands the speech of the mountains, and that they understand his speech and repeat after him. So the mountains have a language and speech which Allah made known to His Prophet Dawud.

We have dealt with the question of the glorification of inanimate things when we addressed His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44], and we returned the view of one who said it is the glorification of state (tasbih al-hal) and not glorification of speech (tasbih al-maqal), because Allah said: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44]. Since He, glory be to Him, has ruled that we do not understand their glorification, it is glorification by speech.

Those who spoke of glorification by indication (tasbih al-dalalah) found it grave that a mountain should have speech, language and mutual understanding. But does the mountain have speech with you? The mountain has speech with its Lord and Creator, who said: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

So: what is your concern in this matter, and why do you deny it?

Consider His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And the thunder exalts [Allah] with His praise, and the angels from fear of Him﴾ [al-Ra'd: 13]. He combined the glorification of the thunder, which is inanimate, with the glorification of the angels, who are of the kinds of created beings. And where is the point of indication in the glorification of the angels? So why the wonder, when it is established that every thing has a language suited to it? We have seen a language for the hoopoe and a language for the ant, and so on.

So the greatness of our master Dawud is that he understood the language of the mountains, heard their glorification, and their glorification agreed with his glorification. Likewise "and the birds": that is, O birds, echo with Dawud, and repeat the glorification with him.

"And We made iron soft for him": this is another miracle of our master Dawud. And if Allah says several things, and in reality one of them proves true, shall I not believe Him in the other?

So if He, glory be to Him, says ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, we must affirm this and believe that the iron became in the hand of our master Dawud like the clay of potter's clay which children shape however they wish. For some hold that ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ means that Allah taught him that fire melts iron; but if the matter were so, there would be no miracle in it and no distinction over other people.

Iron has many properties and various kinds, and the extent of its importance depends on the extent of its hardness. Because of its importance, Allah sent it down from on high just as He sent down the Books; therefore, in Surat al-Hadid He spoke of the Messengers such as Musa and Isa, peace be upon them, and spoke of the sending down of the Books, and said of iron:

﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people﴾ [al-Hadid: 25].

It is well known that sending down comes from above. Allah sent down the Books, which the Messengers recite to guide the one who is guided and listens; and He sent down iron to deter and restrain the disobedient. In iron there is great might in time of war, and benefits for people in time of peace.

Therefore after it He, exalted is He, said:

﴿And that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]. Supports Him in what? In iron, and in its use in times of war. And our master Dawud, peace be upon him, was given by Allah both this and that: the Book for guidance, and iron for war.

Therefore He said to him: ﴿Make coats of mail, complete﴾ [Saba: 11].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 11:

﴿Make coats of mail, and measure well the links,﴾ That is: wide coats of mail. They are the war gear a soldier wears over the places where he may be struck, especially the chest, because inside it lie the heart and the lungs. He was not told to make an axe or a plough, for example, because those serve the benefits of the earth, whereas God wants what protects the method (manhaj) and deters the disobedient.

Before him, coats of mail were made smooth, so that the sword would glide over them and slip, and might strike another part of the body. They were also made only to the size needed to protect the chest. God taught him to make them wide so that they would protect the largest possible part of the body, and so He said: ﴿Make coats of mail, wide ones.﴾ [Saba': 11].

He also taught him that they should be made in the form of interlocking rings, ﴿and measure well the links﴾ [Saba': 11], meaning: make the interlocking of these rings firm, one within another, so that when a sword falls upon them, it holds on one of them and does not move...

Consider that God, exalted is He, did not first teach His prophet David the means of peace; rather He first taught him the means of war and the preparation of equipment against whoever breaks God's word and deviates from His method. He taught him to prepare against them whatever strength he could muster.

The meaning of ﴿and measure well the links﴾ is: make them with precise measurement and firm weaving...

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And work righteousness. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do.﴾ It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, says to His prophet David: Remember, when you do what you have been commanded, that I am Seeing of your work, Aware of it. This reminder is for a prophet trusted in his conduct, so what about us?

We notice that a worker perfects his work as long as the employer is watching him; if the employer is absent, he neglects the work and cheats. God warns us against this matter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 34, verse 12:

That is, just as We gave David a bounty from Us, and among this bounty was that the mountains would echo his praises along with him, and We made iron soft for him, so likewise was it of God's bounty upon his son Solomon that We subjected the wind to him, and made it obey his command.

It has already been explained that the word al-rih (the wind), when it occurs in the singular, refers to punishment and torment, and when it occurs in the plural, it indicates goodness and mercy. Consider His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind, which left nothing it came upon but rendered it like powder.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 41–42]

And He said:

﴿Rather, it is that which you sought to hasten: a wind in which is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24]

And regarding the winds (in the plural) He said: ﴿And We send the fertilizing winds...﴾ [al-Hijr: 22].

The explanation of this is that the single wind, if it is alone, is a destroying wind, because it comes from one direction. What keeps things upright and preserves their balance is that the winds surround them from every side, so they stand firm. For example, what supports skyscrapers is the air that surrounds them; if you drain the air from one side of them, they collapse toward that side. Therefore a single wind is of the kind of punishment, and winds (in the plural) are of the kind of mercy. Do you not see that hurricanes destroy because they come from a single direction?

But, did God, may He be exalted, subject the winds to Solomon, or did He subject the wind to him? They said: The winds were not all subjected to Solomon; rather, He subjected to him a specific wind, which He assigned to him and made obedient to his command, and this wind gave Solomon, peace be upon him, might and invincibility, such that no one could prevail against him or confront him.

Therefore he, peace be upon him, was the prophet and king whom no one fought, and no one dared to dispute his kingdom or his prophethood. How could they, when in his hand was a power not granted to anyone else? His sovereignty was a sovereignty of subjugation: if he willed something, everyone submitted to his will.

As for our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), his call came to win hearts, not to compel bodies. For this reason his Lord addressed him saying:

﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain humbled before it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 4]...

Then the Almighty mentions another matter of what He singled out Solomon, peace be upon him, with: ﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord...﴾ The meaning of ﴿by the permission of his Lord﴾ is that the whole matter was subjection from God to His prophet Solomon, and not a matter originating from himself.

Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever of them deviates from Our command...﴾ i.e., inclines away, or turns aside from it, or disobeys it, ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze.﴾ So Solomon's command to the jinn was from the inner reality of God's command, and whoever disobeys his command has disobeyed Our command.

...the meaning of "Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude" [Saba': 13] is: in gratitude to God for His blessings, not merely so that you may sustain yourselves. Hence: your Lord teaches you: do not work only according to your immediate need, for in your society there are those who are unable to work. So you, who are able, work according to your capacity, take for yourself what suffices you, and give in charity what overflows from you to those who are unable to work. It is well known that gratitude for a blessing secures it, that is, it perpetuates it, and even increases it, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

Or: the meaning of "Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude" [Saba': 13] is: that I enable you to work, so that you may support those who cannot work. "And few of My servants are grateful" [Saba': 13], meaning: few people are those who respond to God's blessing with gratitude.

We said: among the things that God subjected to Solomon, to establish for him a kingship that would not befit anyone after him, was that He subjected the wind to him, and subjected the jinn to him, who worked for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues, etc.

The subjugation of the jinn means that God, glorified and exalted, subjected to him the lightest and most hidden of creatures in movement, and they are the jinn, because the jinn have a distinctive nature. For this reason God said of them: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them﴾ [al-A'raf: 27].

They also have agility in carrying out tasks, in that they shorten the time they take and can carry heavy loads. The evidence for this is that Solomon, peace be upon him, when he asked for the throne of Bilqis, which was in Sheba, said to his assembly: ﴿O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ [al-Naml: 38]. None of the humans spoke, because Solomon had restricted the bringing to a time beyond the capacity of humans. Solomon requested the throne after he had learned that the people of Sheba had set out and were on the way to him, and he wanted someone to bring Bilqis's throne before they reached him.

Even among the jinn, no ordinary jinni took up this task; rather, it was an ifrit (a powerful jinni) who said: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place..."﴾ [al-Naml: 39].

The word ʿifrit (ʿifrīt, a powerful, cunning jinni) means the skilled one among the jinn, the clever one who accomplishes what others of his kind cannot. This shows that among the jinn there are the skilled ifrit and there is the (lubkha), meaning just like us entirely. In our colloquial language we still say: "So-and-so is an ʿifrit," meaning he is skilled, excelling at what others cannot do.

But in Solomon's assembly there was someone more skilled than the ifrit and more experienced and swifter: the one who had been given a measure of knowledge. ﴿The one who had knowledge from the Book said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you..."﴾ [al-Naml: 40].

So if the ifrit would bring the throne of Bilqis before Solomon rose from his place, and Solomon might remain in his place for an hour or several hours, the one who had knowledge from the Book pledged that he would bring it ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ [al-Naml: 40], and the return of a glance does not require a long time, for the eye blinks several times in a single minute.

For this reason, the Truth, glorified be He, depicted the swiftness of response to this act, saying: ﴿And when he saw it placed beside him, he said, "This is from the favour of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."﴾ [al-Naml: 40].

The context does not elaborate on the details of bringing the throne, and does not even mention that Solomon ordered it to be brought; rather: ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you. And when he saw it placed beside him...﴾ [al-Naml: 40], directly like this, because the act itself took no time, and likewise the expression came swiftly and directly.

The Truth, glorified be He, knows that the jinn used to eavesdrop (istirāq al-samʿ) before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). But after his mission (ﷺ), God prevented them from eavesdropping, and He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Whoever listens now will find for himself a watching flame﴾ [al-Jinn: 9].

This is one of the distinctions of his mission (ﷺ): before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), part of the heaven was guarded; after him (ﷺ), all of the heaven was guarded. Before the Messenger of God, the jinn would ascend into the heaven eavesdropping, snatching some of the speech of the angels, and then they would inspire it to their allies among the human devils, as He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you...﴾ [al-An'am: 121].
