Those who were arrogant will say: ﴿Did we turn you away from the guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.﴾ That is, "We did not prevent you from guidance, and we did not stand between you and faith." ﴿Rather, you were criminals﴾ means: by your own nature. You found our path easy, and our worship involves no burden and no accountability; there is no fasting, no prayer, and no zakat in it. Had you thought and used your minds, you would not have followed us.

This is the very logic of Satan when he debates his followers on the Day of Resurrection, and says to them:

﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

This is a continuation of the back-and-forth argument, each side throwing responsibility onto the other. When they (the followers) accused the leaders of criminality, and that they had been led astray by them out of desire for a light religiosity with no obligations and no method restraining their desires, the oppressed (al-mustad'afun) replied: ﴿Nay, but it was your scheming by night and day﴾ [Saba: 33]. That is: the scheming that arises at night, and the scheming that arises by day, when you spent night and day urging us and beguiling us with words until we followed you.

﴿When you were bidding us to disbelieve in God and to set up rivals to Him﴾ [Saba: 33]. That is: partners. ﴿And they will conceal their remorse when they see the punishment﴾ [Saba: 33]. Remorse grips them, yet they do not openly express it or reveal it, lest others gloat over them. There is a difference between a person who regrets and one whose circumstances compel him to make his regret public.

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And We will put shackles upon the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba: 33]. Al-aghlal (the shackles) are the restraints. The meaning of ﴿Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba: 33] is an admonition to the believers who hear these words and this retribution: beware lest tenderness toward these people, because of their state in the Hereafter, take hold of you. Consider what they did in the world of criminal conduct, so that you may know that God, exalted is He, is just and does not wrong people, but they wrong themselves.

An example of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29], up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 36].

That is because when a crime reaches its time's end and its effects subside, people forget its heinousness and remember only the severity of the punishment for it, or the hearts of those who did not witness the crime soften toward the criminal. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, reminds us of His justice, and that this retribution is a fitting recompense. So let not compassion for the criminals take hold of you, and do not show them mercy in this shameful, humiliating situation; set their punishment before their crime, the day they denied the messengers.

Then the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And We did not send a warner to any town except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with..."﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 34, verse 34:

We note in this verse that it mentions warning (nadhara) but does not mention good news (bushara). Why? They said: because the discussion concerns a town in which corruption has spread so widely that nothing remains for it but warning. These are a people who denied the messengers and took a stance of hostility and obstinacy toward the call. As for good news, it comes in the general call, whereas the discussion here concerns a particular call addressed to these deniers...

His saying ﴿إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَا﴾ [Saba': 34] — "mutrafun" is the plural of "mutraf," and "taraf, yatraf" means: lived in luxury (tana''ama). As for "atraf," it means that blessing overpowered him and tempted him. Allah, glorified is He, does not prevent His servant from enjoying His blessings; the important thing is that blessing does not make him rebellious.

Luxury and comfort may also be a gradual lead-on (istidraj) from Allah to the servant, a respite (imla') granted to him, and an extension of blessing for him until he transgresses through it...

The words of the Exalted: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَا إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ كَافِرُونَ﴾ — Why are you disbelievers in what the messengers brought?

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wants of His servants that the strong not domineer over the weak, that the rich not domineer over the poor, and that the learned not domineer over the ignorant. Rather, He wants good to prevail, so whoever possesses a quality of goodness extends it to others.

As for these people, they chose disbelief and were content with it, because blessing made them rebellious and luxurious. They inclined toward arrogance and injustice until they came to love all of this. So when the religion came to correct their conduct, they clashed with it and tried to obliterate it and eliminate its call, because they had grown accustomed to leadership and to tyranny, and they did not want this leadership to be taken from them. Had the world been upright and balanced, there would have been no need for messengers. Thus no messenger came except after corruption had spread and covered everything.

We have previously said that Allah created in the human soul an innate faith-immunity as a result of the original nature (fitrah), but desires and the traditions of the oppressors obliterate this nature, so it needs a reminder (mudhakkir) to return it to the nature and disposition with which Allah created it. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 21], meaning: you are not an originator...

Their saying ﴿إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ كَافِرُونَ﴾ — with what were the messengers sent? They were sent first with the matter of tawhid, that there is no god but Allah; they were sent with the conveyance of the message from Allah; they were sent with miracles; they were sent with rulings and methods that govern the movement of life. These people disbelieved in all of this because they wanted to live in their luxury and their injustice, and to act tyrannically as they pleased.

But their saying ﴿بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ﴾ indicates their stupidity, for they did not say, for example, "with what you have brought," or "with what you claimed," but "with what you were sent with." Thus they acknowledge that they were sent. This is a word of truth that Allah caused to flow upon their tongues, just as He caused it to flow upon their tongues in their saying: ﴿لَا تُنفِقُوا عَلَىٰ مَنْ عِندَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7], and in their saying when revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah: "Indeed the Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him."

So: they acknowledge to the Messenger of Allah his messengerhood, and the one who is sent is not sent by someone like himself but from a higher source; so the message is not from Muhammad;

We have said that religion came to create balance in society, and a unity of belief, economy, and social life. The reasoning of these disbelievers who rejected the messengers is that they have no need for any of this, since they have wealth and children and all the pleasures of life.

﴿And they said...﴾ That is, among the grounds of their disbelief: ﴿We have more wealth and children.﴾ Moreover, their delusion carries them further, so that they say: ﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ Why? They say: because God would not have given us this bounty in this world and withheld it from us in the next.

But we say to them: you are deluded. There is a difference between the gift of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ al-rubūbiyyah) and the gift of divinity (ʿaṭāʾ al-ulūhiyyah). God gives you through the gift of lordship, which encompasses everyone, believer and disbeliever, obedient and disobedient. The gift of divinity, however, is a responsibility. So God gives you in this world by the gift of lordship, and He punishes you in the next by the requirement of divinity.

And this ground they cite, ﴿We have more wealth and children,﴾ is an argument against them, not for them. From where did you get this good? Furthermore, abundance of wealth should have moved you toward paths of goodness, and abundance of children should have made them [a help] to you in the truth. So your disbelief after these blessings is evidence that you used them in falsehood, in wrongdoing and in tyranny.

Their saying, ﴿And we will not be punished,﴾ resembles the saying of the owner of the garden: ﴿I do not think the Hour will ever come; and even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return.﴾ [al-Kahf: 36] This is insolence over the blessing of God and delusion through it. There is no kinship or lineage between God and any of His creation, that He should bless them in this world and bless them in the next without works. These people are tested by wealth and tested by offspring.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 36:

Meaning (say), as a rebuttal to them in their deception by the abundance of wealth and children: ﴿Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it.﴾ [Saba': 36] "Yabsutu" (extends): He widens provision by His generosity. "Yaqdiru" (restricts): meaning He narrows it for whom He wills by His wisdom, exalted is He. Provision is one of the necessary requirements of the lordship (rububiyyah) which created, and which called man into existence, so it must guarantee for him the means of his life.

However, the Provider, glorified is He, does not give provision to people all alike (bi-mistarah), meaning equally, because Allah, exalted is He, wants societies to be cooperative and interdependent. Had every person had what was sufficient for him, no one would have needed anyone else, and this interconnection and collective linkage within society would not have come about.

We have previously explained that the bond of society must be a bond of need, not a bond of favour (tafaddul). Suppose we all graduated from university or obtained doctorates: who would (sweep) the streets, and who would polish shoes? If we made these tasks a favour from some of us to others, no one would accept them.

We also said: if the arrogant or proud man, the pasha, returned to his home and found a foul smell in it, and asked, and they said: "The sewage is such-and-such," there is no doubt he would not rest until this problem was resolved, and perhaps he would get into his car and go himself to the plumber to free him from this problem.

We say in this case: the plumber is superior to the pasha at this time, because Allah gave him a capability over himself that the pasha or the doctorate holder does not possess, and this plumber would only have undertaken such work out of his need for it, otherwise he would not have accepted it.

Therefore the poet well said:

"People, to people, whether of the desert or the town, are servants to one another, even if they do not perceive it."

This service rests upon rotation (tadawul). Allah, exalted is He, has not made one offspring entirely servants and another entirely served; rather you are a servant in one thing and served in another, and thus we are all servants and all served. So that a person, whoever he is, knows that he is a son of circumstances (abghar), and that his sovereignty is not intrinsic to him. If he is above someone, he must appreciate that height and work to maintain his height; if he sees one lower than himself, he should not despise him, but should appreciate his task in serving him, and that he will need him one day in a work he himself cannot do.

Therefore the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision...﴾ [al-Nahl: 71]. Many think that provision is money, but provision is a general word meant to include everything from which a person benefits. Allah, exalted is He, has favoured some of us over others in these things, but which favours? And over whom is one favoured? You are favoured in what you have a talent for, and favoured over others in what you have no talent for. Thus society joins together and completes itself, and is bound by a bond of need, not a bond of favour.

Consider His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for man, when his Lord tries him and honours him and blesses him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me."﴾ [al-Fajr: 15] — thankfully, and may Allah increase your good, in that you attributed honour to your Lord. ﴿But as for when He tries him and restricts his provision for him, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ [al-Fajr: 16] Then the Truth says (kalla): meaning, you are a liar in this statement, because extending provision is not proof of honouring, nor is restricting it a proof of humiliation. Otherwise, how could extending provision be a proof of honour, when people, in what they are provided with, do not honour the orphan with it, nor the needy, and they devour the inheritance greedily? ﴿Nay, but you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the needy, and you devour the inheritance, devouring greedily, and you love wealth with abundant love.﴾ [al-Fajr: 17-20]

So: man must show good manners with Allah in what He has done, because Allah knows how to provide, and He, glorified is He, wants to make of people an example for people. The wealthy one who committed injustice with his wealth, Allah leaves him until the poor one he wronged sees in him the punishment of Allah, so that he knows that Allah has divinity (uluhiyyah), and that Allah has self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah), and the wrongdoer does not escape its punishment in this world before the Hereafter. Allah addressed this meaning to His Prophet, saying: ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you in death, to Us they will return.﴾ [Ghafir: 77]

Furthermore, the matter of provision does not depend on skill, cleverness, or knowledge. There is one who strove for provision, sowed and exerted himself, but at harvest a calamity came upon his crop and destroyed it. As if the Truth, glorified is He, is saying to us: beware lest you notice the divinity of causes and neglect the divinity of the Causer.

Provision is apportioned to its owner, even if another carries it. The fetus in its mother's womb has its nourishment from her constitution and from her blood, but this blood, though the mother carries it, is not her provision; the proof is that when pregnancy occurs, this blood is made available for the fetus's nourishment, and if pregnancy does not occur, this blood is discharged from her in menstruation and the mother does not benefit from it. Why? Because it is not her provision. This helps us understand His saying: ﴿We provide for them and for you.﴾ [al-Isra': 31]

Therefore they said: not everything you possess is provision for you; rather your provision is what you benefit from. A thing may be in your possession and in your holding, you think it is yours, then it is lost from you, or stolen, or nationalised, or struck by a calamity... etc. Indeed, more than that, it may be food that you actually eat, and it becomes blood in your body flowing in your veins, then it flows out of you because of a wound or a surgical operation, for example. So this blood is not provision for you.

The believer should therefore be reassured regarding the process of provision, and know that it is by the self-subsistence of Allah, who provides for both the believer and the disbeliever, and that provision is apportioned to you, named by your name, so no one else may take it, whoever he is. If it is extended for you, praise Allah; and if it is restricted and constricted upon you, know that it is by the wisdom of Allah, and recite: ﴿And there is nothing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We send it down only in a known measure.﴾ [al-Hijr: 21]

Then the verse is concluded with His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ [Saba': 36]. So the majority do not know the wisdom of Allah in the disparity of provisions, and this means that a minority among them are those who know. O Allah, make us among this minority.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position, except one who believes...﴾.

The discourse here is addressed to the disbelievers who wronged themselves with their wealth and their children. Such wealth and such children can never bring one closer to God. But if they are employed in seeking God's pleasure, in the way of God and in the paths of goodness, they are among the greatest means of drawing near to Him.

Wealth is spent in the various channels of good, and children are raised with sound upbringing so that they become a good example in their society. For this reason God, exalted is He, made an exception, saying: ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [Saba': 37], meaning: in what God has granted them of the blessing of wealth and the blessing of children.

﴿Those will have a double reward for what they did﴾ [Saba': 37]. Thus God opened the door to blessing when it is employed in seeking God's pleasure. Not every wealth and not every child is a blessing. Wealth may drag its owner to ruin and cast him into the Fire, and the children whom you thought would be a source of strength and power for you may turn that strength against you.

We have seen many who seek this strength in falsehood, but God wants to humble them through what they were tempted by. A man, for example, goes to propose to a daughter of a notable, or a wealthy man, or one of the holders of high office, for his son, and he rejoices in this lineage and takes pride in it. But can you guarantee that you will please this girl? And that you will never disagree with her one day? Therefore this strength and this standing often turn against our friend, and God humbles him from the very direction in which he thought honour and dignity lay.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So those will have a double reward﴾ [Saba': 37]. The doubling comes only in the reward of a good deed. As for an evil deed, it is not multiplied; it is requited only with its like. This is one of God's mercies to us. He said ﴿the doubling﴾ [Saba': 37] and did not say "multiples," because "al-Ḍi'f" (the double, doubling) is a noun of genus that fits both the few and the many. An example of this is His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr: 1–3]. Here He made an exception with ﴿those﴾ (alladhīna), which is a plural form, while the word for mankind (al-insān) is singular, because it is a noun of genus.

Al-ḍi'f (doubling) means the multiplication of a good deed or the multiplication of a charity. One of the meanings of doubling is that if you weigh the principal you spent, you will find it small in comparison with the reward you received for it.

The multiplication is not the final limit of God's giving, because the noble Prophetic hadith completes this matter. He (ﷺ) said:

Then God, exalted is He, multiplies for whom He wills according to the intentions behind the giving and the spending. One person gives and in his heart he feels that he has given and expended from his wealth and his effort, while another gives and believes that he is merely a conduit on behalf of God, so the wealth in his view is God's wealth and the giving is from God.

Among the examples of giving is what we have learned from Lady Fāṭimah. It is related that our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), entered upon her and found her polishing a dirham of hers. The Messenger of God asked her about it, and she said: "Because I intended to give it in charity, and I know that it falls into God's hand before it falls into the hand of the poor."

Then, the one who gives charity, as soon as he takes it out of his hand, its value leaves his heart; he does not follow it up, and his soul does not cling to it. But when one lends a loan, his soul does not forget it and clings to it, and every time his soul stirs to seek the loan back, he restrains himself, and so he has a reward for his loan each time he exercises patience over it.

For this reason the orientalists (al-mustashriqūn, Western scholars of Islam) raised an uproar over the question of the reward for charity and for loans, and they claimed that the verse and the hadith contradict each other on this matter. In the hadith the Prophet (ﷺ) said, and the Truthful, exalted is He, says: ﴿Who is it that would lend to God a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

By combining the two, a loan is multiplied by twenty, not by eighteen. Praise be to God, God has opened for us what had been closed in this matter. We said: if a man gives a dinar in charity, for example, God rewards him with ten times its like. But has the dinar he paid been returned to him? No. Rather, the dinar went in exchange for the ten. So in reality he received nine, and when it is multiplied, it amounts to eighteen.

Let us return to His saying: ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [Saba': 37]. In many places in the Book of God, God combines faith and righteous deeds. Why? Because they are two wings, and a deed is not completed except by both together. Righteous deeds without faith are dust (habā') with no value, like the charitable deeds of the disbelievers, for which they receive their reward in this world in the form of fame, honour, and perpetuation of their name, but they have no share in the reward of the Hereafter. Likewise, faith has no value if it is not translated into righteous deeds.

﴿So those﴾ [Saba': 37], that is, those who believed and did righteous deeds, ﴿will have a double reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the upper chambers﴾ [Saba': 37]. The "ghurfāt" (upper chambers) is the plural of ghurfah, which is a room built above the house, specially for private retreat. That is why even now, in building villas for example, they make the ground floor for general reception and for meals, while if the homeowner wants to rest, he goes up to the upper floor, which is designed for privacy and seclusion.

Human beings have private matters even within their own homes and among their children. If the homeowner, for example, is in his bedroom, he is free to wear what he wishes, or even to sit in it naked. But if he wants to go out to the living room, he prepares himself and puts on the clothes appropriate to it, and if he wants to go out to the street, he likewise prepares himself with the clothing suited to that. The same applies to the club or the place where people gather: each has its own dress and its own manner.

For the sake of this independence and privacy, people now make a room for the boys and a room for the girls, and if there is not enough space, they place one bed for the boy and one bed for the girl.

God, exalted is He, preserves His servant's dignity and preserves this privacy for him, a privacy that is safe, whose safety is not disturbed by fear: ﴿and they will be secure in the upper chambers﴾ [Saba': 37].

These people strove against Allah's signs to turn people away from them and to distract them from listening to them.

As for "mu'ajizin" (مُعَاجِزِينَ), its singular is mu'ajiz. The word al-mu'ajazah is on the pattern of mufa'alah (a form expressing reciprocal action), meaning that one party tries to overcome the other, that is, wants to defeat him. So al-mu'ajazah is a contest. But do not think that it is only between believers and disbelievers, or between the messengers and those who denied them. No, it is a far greater contest. Those who contend against Allah, contend against Him regarding His signs, seeking to nullify them and to place obstacles in their path. However great their scheming, they will never overpower Allah, and they will never escape from Him, glorified is He, as He said: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, with no escape, and they are seized from a nearby place﴾ [Saba': 51].

Here He says: ﴿Those will be brought forward into the punishment﴾. The meaning of "muhdarun" (مُحْضَرُونَ) is that they will be brought forcibly, against their will. It is the passive participle of hadara, so they are dragged and pulled like those who have been seized...

Say: "My Lord expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it for him." Here "yabsut" means He widens it, and "yaqdir" means He constricts it. This meaning appeared several verses earlier, but here it adds a new nuance. Immediately after, He says: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. It is as if the Exalted is drawing our attention to the fact that all creation is His creation and His servants, and He is able to give to everyone and to widen provision for everyone. But He wills that creation love one another and that people support one another. Therefore He widened for some of them and restricted for others. Then He pointed to the one whom He widened upon and hinted to him the reward for spending, so that he would spend on his brother who has been restricted.

This verse gives us a summary of the economy of the whole world, because the meaning of economy is balancing expenditures with incomes. Expenditures have a place to be spent, and incomes have a source coming in. Thus, there must necessarily be in one place a group that gives and a group that takes. Therefore the Exalted did not leave the expansiveness of wealth free in this manner, nor did He leave the restriction of the poor [unaddressed]; rather He made for this a place of giving and for that a source.

So after the Exalted had informed: ﴿Say, "Indeed my Lord expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him"﴾, He stated its ruling, saying: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾. The Exalted observes the principle of utility for the owner of wealth, and observes the love of the rich for wealth; therefore He reassures them about their wealth, and He Himself undertakes to replace it for them.

The Exalted expanded provision for the rich, and they love wealth, but He says to them: "If you are referred (uhilta) to a wealthy one, then follow" (idha uhilta 'ala ghaniyy fa-tba'), meaning: if you have a debt owed by a poor person, and he refers you to his debt on a wealthy person able to pay, then transfer it, because you do not know when Allah will widen provision for the poor man to settle what he owes.

Thus Allah reassured the rich that their wealth will not diminish by spending, because it has been referred to Allah, and He has undertaken the settlement.

Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) teaches us, saying: "You have of your wealth only what you eat and finish, or wear and wear out, or give in charity and preserve."...

Therefore the verse is concluded with His saying: ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾. He, glorified be He, said "the best of providers" because the provider (al-raziq) is everyone who extends his hand to you with that from which you benefit. Accordingly, your father is a provider for you, and the one who supports you and takes responsibility for you is a provider; likewise your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is a provider. But there is a difference between them: your father is a provider because he brings you provision, but if you ask him where this provision comes from, he says: from Allah. So he is a means and a conveyer. As for the Exalted, He is the creator of provision; therefore He said ﴿and He is the best of providers﴾.

We have previously explained: when you see a shared attribute between the creature and the Creator, know that the aspect is distinct, and each has what suits it. Accordingly, the aspect of excellence here is that He, the Exalted, is the Provider, and He is the creator of provision, and He is the One who facilitates for you its causes until it reaches you.

And it has been said: Allah's excellence in provision arises from three matters. The first: He, glorified be He, does not postpone provision until the time of need for it; rather He created it for you before He created you, and prepared for you the means of life before He summoned you to it. The second: He does not hold you accountable for what He has provided you. The third: He does not ask you for reward for what He has bestowed upon you.

For all this, the Exalted was and still is the best of providers...

Meaning: Remember the Day when He will gather them all together. The "Day" is a time-frame for the gathering and the assembling on the Day of Resurrection. But why does the Qur'an mention this day? They said: here there is an indication to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that Allah has not forgotten him, nor abandoned him, nor left him alone. The proof is that He will avenge him against his enemies and deniers on this day, as if Allah were saying to him: "You will see what We will do to them," just as He, glorified is He, said at the end of Surat al-Mutaffifin: ﴿Has the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 36].

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?"﴾ It is known that the disbelievers worshipped many deities, so why did He single out the angels for this question here? They said: because they are the highest of the kinds that were worshipped besides Allah and the closest of them to Allah; for this reason they said of them, "the daughters of Allah." They thought that the angels have a word with Allah and that they could intercede for them or defend them if they worshipped them. Therefore the angels are mentioned here, and the tree and the stone that were worshipped besides Him, glorified is He, are not mentioned.

But why was the question addressed to the angels who were worshipped, and not to the worshippers who associated partners with Allah? Why did Allah not rebuke and reproach them for worshipping other than Him? They said: because the Truth, glorified is He, wanted the polytheists to hear the reply from the angels themselves, so that the proof against them would be more conclusive.

The meaning: Remember the day when He gathers them all together. "The day" is the time-frame for the gathering and the assembling, the Day of Resurrection. But why does the Messenger of God mention this day? They said: here is an indication to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that God has not forgotten him, nor abandoned him, as is evident from the fact that He will avenge him against his enemies and deniers on this day, as if God is saying to him: "You will see what We will do to them," just as He said, glorified is He, at the end of al-Mutaffifin: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 36].

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then He will say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?"﴾ [Saba: 40]. It is well known that the disbelievers worshipped many deities, so why did He single out the angels here for this question? They said: Because they are the highest of the kinds that were worshipped besides God and the closest of them to God; therefore they said about them, "the daughters of God." They think the angels have a word with God, and that they may intercede for them or defend them if they worship them. Therefore the angels are mentioned here, and the trees and stones that were worshipped besides Him, glorified is He, are not mentioned.

But why was the question directed to the angels who were worshipped, and not to the worshippers who associated others with God? Why did God not rebuke and reproach them for worshipping others besides Him? They said: Because the Truth, glorified is He, wanted the polytheists to hear the reply from the angels themselves, so that the proof against them would be more conclusive.

He, glorified is He, says to the angels: ﴿Did these [al-Musharikun, the polytheists]﴾ [Saba: 40] ﴿—"Did these used to worship you?"﴾ [Saba: 40]. So their first reply is ﴿They will say: "Glory be to You!"﴾ [Saba: 41], meaning: an declaration of Your transcendence, O Lord, that anyone be worshipped besides You. ﴿"You are our Guardian, not them"﴾ [Saba: 41], meaning: we, in our servitude to You, O Lord, are more honoured and more dignified than that they should worship us. ﴿"Rather, they used to worship the jinn"﴾ [Saba: 41], meaning: they did not worship us; rather, they worshipped the jinn. ﴿"Most of them believed in them."﴾ [Saba: 41]. So why did they worship the jinn? And why were most of them believers in the jinn?

The jinn are the kind that stands opposite mankind, and they were named "jinn" because they are hidden from us: they see us while we do not see them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you cannot see them﴾ [al-A'raf: 27].

Those who worshipped the jinn did not worship all of them; rather, they worshipped the devils among them, and they worshipped them because they obeyed them. And most of them were believers in the jinn. Why? Because the jinn used to eavesdrop, picking up some news and facts, then they would convey them to their allies among the devils of mankind, who would take them and inform people of them as though they knew the unseen. However, they would mix into these facts much falsehood. Then some events would come in agreement with what they had reported, and people would be seduced by them and think they knew the unseen.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So on this Day, none of you will have power to benefit or harm another...﴾.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi on surah 34 (Saba'), verse 42:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day﴾ [Saba': 42], meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿none of you will have power to benefit or harm another﴾ [Saba': 42], meaning the angels and those among the polytheists who worshipped them. If they imagined that the angels were honoured servants, and that they had a rank with God, and so would intercede (shafa'ah) for them, then they are told: you do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and you do not intercede on your own initiative, but you wait until you are permitted to intercede. Then, O angels, you would be ashamed to be intercessors for one who worshipped other than God, because your sincerity in your servitude to God Almighty prevents you from supporting these people or interceding for them.

A similar situation we have witnessed with the Master of the Messengers, may God bless him and grant him peace, where those who believed in God but rejected His Messenger were placed before him ahead of those who disbelieved in God. Thus the zeal of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his Lord was greater than his zeal for himself.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will say to those who did wrong: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [Saba': 42]. This verse is among the places where the orientalists stood, thinking that there is a objection to the words of God. They said: the Qur'an says in Saba': ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [Saba': 42], and it says in as-Sajdah: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [as-Sajdah: 20].

So did the disbelievers deny the Fire, or did they deny the punishment? We say: among them were those who denied the existence of the Fire altogether, and to these God said ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [Saba': 42], because their denial was directed at the Fire, and the relative pronoun (الَّتِي, allatī, feminine) refers back to the Fire.

As for those who believed in the existence of the Fire but denied that they would be punished by it, God said to them ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [as-Sajdah: 20], because their denial was of the punishment, not of the Fire; therefore the relative pronoun (الَّذِي, alladhī, masculine) came referring back to the punishment.

Then the Truthful, exalted is He, says:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say: "This is not..."﴾.

... If Muhammad were a sorcerer who bewitched those who believe in him, as you claim, then why did he not bewitch you too, so that this matter would end? And it is well known that the one who is bewitched has no choice with the sorcerer. So then: this saying of theirs is a lie against our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and stubbornness and arrogance in refusing to accept the truth that he brought.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 34, verse 44:

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is asking: from where did they obtain this speech, and these accusations? Did We give them books which they study, and from which they know that?

He, glorified is He, answers: ﴿And We did not give them any books which they could study﴾ [Saba': 44], and ﴿We did not send to them before you any warner﴾ [Saba': 44], meaning: a messenger who would inform them of this. So then: from where did they get it?

He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach one-tenth of what We had given them...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 45:

The meaning: what they said about the Messenger of Allah, and about the guidance he brought, is denial, just as the earlier peoples denied. It is a established way (sunnah muttaba'ah) and a constant nature among those to whom messengers are sent: when a new religion comes to bring them out of their tyranny and arbitrary rule, and to end their dominion and their enslavement of people, they inevitably confront the religion and deny the messengers, so that the means of tyranny and the means of corruption may remain in their hands.

So the meaning of ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبلِهِمْ﴾ ("and those before them denied") is the earlier nations who denied your brothers the previous messengers. So you, O Muhammad, are no novelty in this.

﴿وَمَا بَلَغُواْ مِعْشَارَ مَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ ("and they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them"): meaning, the earlier nations who denied their messengers did not reach, in messengership, in method, in proof and in clear evidence, a tenth of what We have given you. That is because our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), brought the complete religion and the perfect method, which cannot be improved upon.

Or: the meaning is that ﴿وَمَا بَلَغُواْ﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah who denied the Messenger of Allah, ﴿مِعْشَارَ مَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾, meaning: a tenth of what We gave the earlier nations of strength. The nations that denied the messengers were stronger, more influential and more civilized than the disbelievers of Makkah. And where are they from ʿAd, Thamud and Pharaoh?...

So where is the strength of the Quraysh disbelievers compared with the strength of those who are proverbial for strength, force, tyranny and oppression? Yet the punishment of Allah struck them anyway.

Al-miʿshār (مِعْشَار, a tenth) is more than al-ʿashīr (عَشِير, a tenth of a hundred...), and al-ʿashīr is more than al-ʿushr (عُشْر, a tenth). So if you mean tens you say ʿushr, if you mean hundreds you say ʿashīr, and if you mean thousands you say miʿshār.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 46:

After Allah, the Exalted, has given them a lesson and a warning through those deniers who came before them, He returns to address them afresh, saying to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Say" (qul), meaning to them: ﴿I only admonish you with one thing﴾. Admonition (al-wa'z) is not the establishment of a new ruling; rather, it is a reminder of a ruling that has already passed and that people have forgotten. The admonisher (al-wa'iz) makes clear to people matters that they already know and believe in from the religion, but desires and heedlessness have caused them to forget these matters, so he reminds them of them. Admonition comes only from one who loves you and is keen for your good.

Therefore, Allah, blessed and exalted, gives us a model of admonition in the story of Luqman when he admonishes his son: ﴿And when Luqman said to his son, while he was instructing him: "O my dear son, do not associate anything with Allah..."﴾ [Luqman: 13].

The meaning of "with one thing" (bi-wahidah) is: one admonition that contains all the single matters. The context uses "only" (innama), which denotes restriction (al-qasr), meaning: I do not admonish you except with one thing. What is it? ﴿That you stand up for Allah﴾. That is: beware of standing up for the desire of your own self, or for a leadership you wish to preserve, beware of standing up while you intend to exalt yourself over this Prophet. Rather, your standing should be for Allah, meaning you strip yourself of your whims, strip yourself of your desires and of your partisanship.

And since they are being addressed to stand for Allah, there must be a status of Allah in their hearts, and He, glory be to Him, is in their minds, as evidenced by: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say: "All praise is for Allah."﴾ [Luqman: 25].

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 87].

So: they used to believe that Allah, the Exalted, is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth, because this matter is so clear that no denier denies it, however far disbelief and atheism may go...

The standing intended here does not require a group or a crowd, because it is a standing for reflection (tafakkur). It should be ﴿in pairs and singly﴾. "In pairs" (mathnā) means two by two, and "singly" (furādā) means one by one, so that each one withdraws with himself to ponder the affair of Muhammad with objectivity and detachment: how he was among you, what his conduct and character were, whether you ever caught him in a lie, sorcery, or soothsaying, whether he had ever claimed what was not his, and whether you saw in him before his mission any sign of madness. Then ﴿you may reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾.

This reflection on the state of the Messenger of Allah requires objectivity, which is why He chose that they be alone with it, either in pairs or singly. A person who is by himself has no equal before whom he is defeated, nor one who incites him to other than the truth, so his opinion in this state is closer to correctness.

The one who reflects alone reaches the truth, because he will not deceive himself, nor cheat himself, nor be too proud to return to the truth. If they are a group, each of them must try to prove his argument, even if he is compelled to lie and deceive, as we see in such situations: each one swears that he is upon the truth and the other is upon falsehood.

Thus this method of thinking protects us and saves us from the mob mentality of the crowd in judgment, the mob mentality we see, for example, in demonstrations, where each shouts what he wants, the voices mix, and the chants overlap, so that you cannot distinguish them...

So the truth teaches us how to reflect in pairs or singly, and protects us from mob mentality...

Likewise, if they are in pairs, then the two, as we say, are "the opinion and the other opinion." If one of them is defeated before the other, his defeat is concealed. Therefore we always hear someone say to his opponent: "I want you and me to sit alone?" Because you two are the parties to the matter, and there is no third party who would cause either of you embarrassment or humiliation, or cause you to change your conduct before him.

The meaning of "that you stand up for Allah" is not the standing that is opposed to sitting. Rather, whoever undertakes a matter, meaning does it and performs it, even if he is seated, is said to "stand" by it. From this we say: "So-and-so stands by the affair of so-and-so," or "So-and-so performs the duty of so-and-so," meaning he carries it out.

The meaning of ﴿your companion﴾ is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿madness﴾ meaning insanity, because they said of the Messenger of Allah that he was mad. It is strange of them, when they are the most knowledgeable of people about him, to describe him as mad, when they never observed in him any sign of madness and he never did anything contrary to the society in which he lived. Rather, before the mission they used to call him "the truthful, the trustworthy." Just as their lie was shown in their saying "sorcerer," so their lie was shown in their saying "madman."

If any one of them were to be alone with himself and then reflect on the person of the Messenger of Allah, he would reach the truth on his own. And if he turned over in his mind these accusations, he would find that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is innocent of them. And as long as he is alone in this reflection, he will never be ashamed to return to the truth, because he will not be defeated before anyone...

Allah, the Exalted, has not mentioned to us the result of this reflection and investigation, in pairs or singly, because it is known and clear. However, He said about him (ﷺ): ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.﴾

Another point: did all the people believe in the Messenger of Allah after they heard from him the miraculous Qur'an, so that we could say the Qur'an is the miracle that proves the truthfulness of the Messenger? We say: no. Some of them did not believe after hearing the Qur'an, and some of them believed before the Qur'an was revealed, as soon as Muhammad said: "I am the Messenger of Allah." The first of them was Lady Khadijah and al-Siddiq Abu Bakr. So what was the basis (haythiyyah) of their belief in the Messenger of Allah? And what miracle did they know his truthfulness by? For these people, the basis and miracle was his conduct (ﷺ) among them first, and that is sufficient for them to believe in him if he says: "I am the Messenger of Allah to you." As for the Qur'an, it is a miracle and a challenge to whoever denies.

Therefore we see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reminding his people of this conduct among them and taking it as his proof. "When he was sent, he ascended al-Safa and called out to the people. When they gathered around him, he said: 'Do you see, if I told you that cavalry behind this valley were coming to raid you, would you believe me?' They said: 'We have never found you to lie.' He said: 'I am the Messenger of Allah to you.' They said to one another: 'You are a liar, may you perish! Is this why you gathered us?'..."

And you notice that those who confronted the Messenger of Allah at the beginning of the mission, and who accused him of lying, were from his own family and the people closest to him, and his uncle was the one who said to him: "May you perish! Is this why you gathered us?" Here is a place of wisdom and proof in the mission of the Messenger of Allah, which Allah made so that people would know that the status and leadership of Quraysh in the Arabian Peninsula did not produce the message of Muhammad so that they might rule the world with it, for his greatest enemies were from Quraysh, and the Messenger of Allah found no support in Makkah; his support was in Yathrib.

Therefore we have previously said: faith in Muhammad is what created solidarity (al-'asabiyyah) for Muhammad, not that solidarity for Muhammad created faith in him (ﷺ).

The reward (al-ajr): it is the wage given in return for work. All the messengers uttered this phrase; Allah taught each of them to say to his people: ﴿And I ask you no reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 109]. It is as if, implicit in this manner of speech, he means: if there were a fair assessment, I would deserve a reward for my message and my call, because I bring you a great benefit through guidance. For it is not a transaction in this transient world; rather it is a lasting benefit in an eternal, everlasting life.

But the reality is that I do not take my reward from you; I take it from Allah, because the work I do is too great for you to price it with a value. The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who assesses my work, and I am certain that He will give me ﴿my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47].

The meaning of ﴿So it is for you﴾ [Saba': 47] is: if I had taken a reward from you, I would work for you with that reward, or its recompense would return to you.

We have already said that all the messengers uttered this phrase except two messengers, in whose speech this phrase did not come: our master Abraham and our master Moses, peace be upon them both. This indicates that this matter is built upon a great and lofty wisdom. So why Abraham and Moses specifically among all the messengers?

It is said: because our master Abraham, peace be upon him, first confronted those who opposed him in his uncle; when his uncle confronted him and rejected his call, he withdrew from him and was content to pray for him. It is not reasonable that he would expect a reward from his uncle; therefore this matter of reward did not come in his speech.

Likewise Moses, peace be upon him, whose first call was to Pharaoh, who said to him: ﴿Did We not bring you up among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 18]. That is: if he deserved a reward for his call to Pharaoh, he would be too shy to ask him for it, since he had been raised in his house and under his care.

The phrase ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you﴾ [Saba': 47] may bear two meanings: that I took a reward and gave it to you, or that I in fact never asked you for any reward. Then the verse concludes with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He is Witness over all things﴾ [Saba': 47], meaning He is a witness over us all, and He knows what I have endured in the cause of calling you to the truth, and He knows the stubbornness and obstinacy you have shown toward me. He, glory be to Him, will magnify my reward in proportion to my suffering and what I have borne in the cause of guiding you and bringing you by the hand to His presence.

If a person who does any work must have some share of it, some gain and benefit, then the Messenger of Allah did not even ask you for a reward for the work; so with what then do you accuse him after this?

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to clarify for us a matter related to the truth that the Messenger of Allah brought. The disbelievers used to object to the person of the Messenger of Allah, as evidenced by their saying: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?..﴾ [Sad: 8], and they said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31].

They acknowledge the Qur'an and know that it is a Reminder, and that there is no fault in it. The problem was that it descended upon this particular man, and did not descend upon one of their great men. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to say that the sending down of Allah's methods to the earth must descend upon a chosen one whom Allah chooses, not a chosen one whom creation chooses. So there is no meaning to their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31].

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, answers them with proof: ﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 32].

And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah knows best where He places His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

The mercy of Allah is that by which people benefit, either in this world, and this is a mercy that encompasses believer and disbeliever, or a mercy in the Hereafter, and this is for the believer and not the disbeliever. This Hereafter mercy is lasting and enduring in bliss that neither escapes you nor do you escape it. So if I am dividing your provisions and livelihood in the life of this world, how would I leave to you the choice of who will show you mercy in the Hereafter? Would I divide among you the temporary mercy and leave to you the everlasting mercy?

Then the Qur'an takes a different course with them after having admonished them and shown them affection, and He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: indeed my Lord hurls the truth...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 34, verse 48:

You may notice here the sharpness of the style, in contrast to the preceding verses, which admonished them and showed them kindness, as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is saying to them: Do not think that We will keep courting you, or that you are the ones who will steer the ships. Rather, God will make His religion prevail despite your obstinacy, and the Truth will rise above your disbelief.

So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, in response to them: ﴿Indeed, my Lord casts the Truth﴾. After He had given you the opportunity, and after your rebellion had lasted long, now my Lord will cast the Truth, as He, glory be to Him, said in another place: ﴿Nay, We cast the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-AnbiyaRPM: 18].

Al-qadhf (casting) is throwing with force, a word that suggests violence and strength when it comes from humans. How much more so when the casting is from God, and what is cast by God is the Truth, which, as we have said, is the thing that is firm and does not change.

Casting necessarily has an aim and a goal. Whoever wants to cast something must determine the distance, whether it is near or far. If the target is near, the thrower rarely misses the thing thrown; but if the target is far, the probability of error is greater, and so on, the more the distance increases. This is because the meaning of casting is fixing a place for the projectile to reach, and to hit the intended goal.

When the place is near, the changes that may affect it are few, because the time for the projectile to reach it is short. By contrast, if the target is far, it is exposed to change: its angle may differ because of the wind, or storms, or the like. Therefore, in this case we need instruments and precise calculations that compute the distance of the target and the force of the projectile, and the force of the wind, meaning what collides with it, and other calculations of speed and time, like one who shoots a bird, for example, while it is in the air: he must change the point of aim to suit the movement and direction of the bird.

No one is more capable of this process than the Knower of the unseen, glory be to Him, from Whose knowledge not an atom's weight escapes in the heavens or on the earth. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, brought the attribute that suits precision in this process, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the Truth, the Knower of the unseen﴾. He, glory be to Him, first casts the Truth, and His casting never misses its target, because He, exalted is He, is the Knower of the unseen.

The Truth that God casts is the method He sent down from heaven. He casts it for an aim, which is the message, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

Thus: the Caster is God, the thing cast is the Truth, which is the firm thing that does not change, and the intended goal is the arrival of the message to the one whom God has chosen for it. This process does not miss, because the Caster knows every unseen matter that affects the course of what is cast. So the Truth must reach its chosen owner and the one selected to bear it, and not anyone else...

The word ﴿al-Ghuyub﴾ (the unseen) here indicates the multitude of influences that may obstruct the projectile and prevent it from reaching its target, and these influences are known only to God.

If you say: the verb ﴿yaqdhifu﴾ (casts) came in the present tense, which indicates both the present and the future, meaning that the Truth, glory be to Him, has the practice of casting the Truth to the messengers, so has He cast it to the Messenger of God?

The answer comes in His saying in the verse after it: ﴿Say: The Truth has come...﴾ [Saba: 49]

Say: "The truth has come." That is, it has been cast into action in the form of the Qur'an, which was sent down to Muhammad, whom God chose for the message and for carrying His method to His creation, so that it may organize the movement of their lives. And if the clear, established truth has come and become manifest, and the One who cast it is the Knower of the unseen, then what is the position of the falsehood that opposes it? It must retreat, and it cannot stand firm before the power of the truth.

"Falsehood can neither originate anything nor bring it back." It does not originate anything in the first instance, nor does it bring anything back in the hereafter. This is like the saying we use: "neither in the caravan nor in the army" (lā fi al-'ayr wa-lā fi al-nafīr)... This is if falsehood has any existence or permanence. Rather, falsehood is nothing but a distant illusion in the minds of its adherents, having no real existence.

We note that the Prophet (ﷺ) attributed any misguidance to the self (nafs), but attributed guidance to God and to the revelation sent down to him. This is because when God sends down a guiding method (manhaj) for a chosen human being, choice (ikhtiyar) operates only where alternatives exist from which reason can select. Reason has no task in a single matter that has no alternative. For example, you say, "I want to travel to al-Fayyum," and you find only one road, so reason and choice have no role here. But if you say, "I want to travel to Alexandria," you find two roads: the agricultural road, with its description and features, and the desert road, with its description and features.

God created His whole cosmos to be chosen, except in the matters of divine decree (al-qadar, predestination), which God made compulsory, with no choice for the human being in them, because his interference in them would corrupt them.

Do not think that you alone are free to choose in the cosmos. Everything around you, of heaven and earth, is also free to choose. However, the heavens, the earth and the mountains chose once, and then they extended that general choice to all the particulars that come after. Read in this regard His saying, ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and the human being bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]

So the inanimate things chose from the beginning to be subdued to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and refused to bear this trust. As for the human being, he bore it and said, "I can by my reason choose among the alternatives." He forgot that he perceived the time of undertaking, but did not perceive the time of performance, nor the accidents, desires, whispering of Satan, and so on that befall him. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, described him as "wrongdoing to himself, ignorant of the consequences," meaning: wrongdoing to himself, ignorant of the outcomes.

The method that God the Truth, glorified is He, established is a general method, set for the believer and the disbeliever alike. God guided and pointed everyone to the path of good and left everyone free to choose. Among them are those who choose the desires of their souls in this world and decide to enjoy them, and whatever happens afterwards happens. And among them are those who contemplate this method and find it, by a miracle, to be obeyed, and this miracle broke the laws of the cosmos. Therefore it is a method from the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the Supreme God, who chose this method for the welfare of creation.

In general, the human being loves good for himself, but people differ in their understanding of good. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man has always been hasty.﴾ [al-Isra: 11]

And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 37]

It is as though the Truth, glorified is He, says to the human being: Do not hasten in your supplication, and be content with what He has chosen for you, because your judgment and understanding of good are according to the extent of your knowledge of good, whereas He knows better than you what is good for you, and better than you how you will receive this good and its effect upon you.

Therefore we have said: we often hear someone say, "I pray and follow God's method, yet I supplicated and it was not answered for me." We say: because you supplicated for good according to your own understanding of good, but your Lord knows better than you what is good for you; therefore He did not respond to your supplication.

Also we often hear a mother, in a moment of anger, supplicate against her only son, saying (May Your fire drink him, may Your news come to me) — by God, if God answered her supplication, what would she be saying about her Lord? So God not answering your supplication at times is in fact the very good for you, because He knows the folly of your supplication, and He is a Lord who does not approve for you the consequences of this folly; therefore He corrects for you what you erred in.

Another matter in this issue: a supplication may be for a true good, but it comes from someone who is not compelled (mudtarr), coming as we say colloquially (casually, without real need). The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, promised to answer the one who is compelled when he calls upon Him, saying, ﴿Or who answers the compelled one when he calls upon Him?﴾ [al-Naml: 62]. So had you been compelled, He would have answered you, because the compelled one has exhausted all the means granted to him by God, and his strength has failed, so he turns to God, the Causer, glorified is He. Most of us call upon God without compulsion.

So: when your supplication is not answered, know that it was a supplication for evil that you thought to be good, and the good lies in God not answering you, or in your supplication being without compulsion.

Let us return to our discussion of the method that God established for guiding all people, and we say: whoever believes in this method and is guided by it, God helps him and increases him in guidance, as He said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ [Muhammad: 17] And whoever turns away from it and goes astray, God likewise increases him in misguidance and seals his heart, so that no faith enters it and no disbelief leaves it, because He, the Exalted, is a Lord who helps His servant in what he loves and increases him in what he wants.

So: as long as there is choice in accepting the method, there must be guidance and there must be misguidance. Guidance brings good and reward, and misguidance brings evil and punishment. Here the Truth, glorified is He, clarifies for us that misguidance is attributed to the self, whereas guidance is attributed to God and to His method. He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from God, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself.﴾ [al-Nisa: 79]

And before it He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: all is from God.﴾ [al-Nisa: 78] Why? Because He made both paths and guided everyone. If you look at the act, then God is the One who supplied you, as He said: ﴿To each — these and those — We extend from the bounty of your Lord, and the bounty of your Lord is not restricted.﴾ [al-Isra: 20]

So God gave you, for example, the tongue, with which you may utter the word of monotheism, or with which you may utter the word of disbelief, God forbid. The tongue did not disobey you, neither in this nor in that. So who gave you the freedom of choice? God. Therefore we say: no disbeliever disbelieves under compulsion from God; as for His being displeased with him, that is another matter.

So we say: a man who gave his son a pound, for example, which is purchasing power, and said to him, "Go to the market and buy with it whatever you want, but it would please me if you spent it on something beneficial," the one who gave him purchasing power is his father, and the one who left him the choice is his father, and he is able to restrain him and strip him of this power. This is choice.

Likewise, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants the human being to come to Him while he is free to choose, and He is able that he not come. He wants the servants to come to Him out of love, desire and faith, not out of compulsion and tyranny, because He, as we have said before, wants hearts that humble themselves, not bodies that submit.

So His saying, ﴿Say: If I go astray﴾ [Saba: 50] means: I and you are equal in this matter, because misguidance is the result of the sins that the self commits, so the self is the cause of misguidance. ﴿Say: If I go astray, I go astray only against myself﴾ [Saba: 50]. As for guidance, it is from God, because it is through the method of God: ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ [Saba: 50].

However, the Prophet (ﷺ) and his community agree in attributing misguidance to the self, but he differs from them in guidance: ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ [Saba: 50]. His guidance came to him (ﷺ) directly from God before He sent him a messenger with the message, and before the revelation was sent down to him, even from the heavens. As for the guidance of the community, it comes through the Messenger, who conveys the method of God and brings the miracle.

So the guidance of the Messenger of God was a beginning, according to what God chose for him as Messenger in this state of guidance. Then He sent down to him the method to guide the community.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Near﴾ [Saba: 50]: "Hearing" means He knows what I seek, and hears from me every breath. And He, glorified is He, despite His hearing, is near to me, not delaying in answering me, because an act from God, exalted is He, does not need treatment or exertion; rather, the act from God is by "Be!"

Then the Truth, glorified is He, turns back to His Messenger (ﷺ) to console him:

﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there is no escape...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi on Surah Saba (34), verse 51:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you could see﴾ [Saba 34:51]. This is a conditional construction (uslub shart) that occurs several times in the Qur'an. You will notice that the context does not mention its response (jawab al-shart, the apodosis). Read: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba 34:31], and ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord..."﴾ [An'am 6:27].

Here the response is omitted because it is understood from the context. The implied meaning is: "And if you could see, O Muhammad, when they are struck with terror on the Day of Resurrection, you would see a great thing and a wondrous matter that would relieve your heart and take vengeance on your behalf for what they did to you in denial and opposition." This same meaning appears in His saying: ﴿Have the disbelievers not been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ [Mutaffifin 83:36].

Those who transgressed and acted arrogantly in the world, who collided with the word of truth, and who were obstinate tyrants and pharaohs, you will see in the Hereafter, when the terror of it strikes them, as (basabis) [i.e., as meek and helpless as] cats and rabbits.

The meaning of ﴿there is no escape﴾ [Saba 34:51] is that there is no place of flight and no salvation for them. A person may be frightened of something yet be able to flee from it, or perhaps someone may rescue him. But these people will be terrified with no rescuer, no way out, and no refuge. This will soothe your heart and the hearts of the believers who were harmed along with you in spreading the call to truth.

Just as they stood against the call of God, so on the Day of Resurrection they will stand in a position of humiliation and disgrace. Reflect on: ﴿made to stand before their Lord﴾ [Saba 34:31], ﴿made to stand over the Fire﴾ [An'am 6:27], and ﴿made to stand before their Lord﴾ [An'am 6:30]. That is, they will wait to be given permission so they may see what their intercessors, whom they worshipped besides God, will say. But they will be surprised to find that their intercessors and their chiefs have gone ahead of them into the Fire and hastened toward the punishment, just as they had preceded them into misguidance.

For this reason He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every sect those who were most insolent toward the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 19:69]. And He says concerning Pharaoh: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them to the Fire; and wretched is the destination to which they are brought﴾ [Hud 11:98].

Thus God despairs them of salvation, because they were waiting for these intercessors and these leaders to defend them, but instead they went ahead of them into the punishment.

These stations we have mentioned for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection each carry their own humiliation, each carry their own terror, and each one is a punishment in itself. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is saying to His Prophet: If you had seen their stations and their terror, it would have quenched your anger, and you would have known that We were able to repay them with what they deserve.

We have previously given an example of this situation: a (fityah) or (faqid), a local strongman who humiliates the people of his town and frightens them, so that everyone fears him, flatters him, and guards against his evil. Once the police arrested him and led him away in chains, and you would see the townspeople rejoicing, pointing at him with winks. In such situations you actually hear someone say, "If only you had seen what happened to so-and-so." The meaning is: you have seen a strange matter that cannot be imagined.

The meaning of ﴿and they will be seized﴾ [Saba 34:51] is that they will be destroyed ﴿from a near place﴾ [Saba 34:51], which is the place of the Resurrection and the site of reckoning. That is, God, glorified is He, does not leave them any room; rather, He takes them from the reckoning straight into the Fire.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him." But how could they obtain [faith] from such a distant place...﴾.

Glory be to God! After they had done to the Messenger of God and his followers what they had done, and after they were seized with terror and the punishment encompassed them, they now proclaim faith and say, ﴿We have believed in Him﴾ [Saba': 52]. This is similar to the faith of Pharaoh when drowning overtook him: ﴿I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of those who submit [to Him]﴾ [Yunus: 90]. God replied to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 91]. That is, this is a time when faith does not benefit.

Here the Truth returns their faith to them, saying: ﴿And how can they reach [such faith] from a far place?﴾ [Saba': 52]. Al-tanawush (the reaching, the taking hold of something with ease) means the taking hold of faith. ﴿From a far place﴾ [Saba': 52]: the word (anna) means "how": how can they have faith now, when they are in the position of death or resurrection? Faith was near to them in the world, but now it is as far from them as can be.

Therefore the context uses the interrogative particle (anna), which has two meanings: it means "how," indicating amazement, that is, this is a strange and wondrous matter on their part. And (anna) may also mean "from where," as in the words of our master Zakariyya to Lady Maryam: ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37].

That is: from where do you have this provision? Therefore, a guardian of affairs should learn from this verse: if he sees among his household something that he did not bring them, he should ask them where they obtained it and how it came to his house, and this is a necessary precaution, because that thing may be a stealthy gain or an enticement to disobedience.

Lady Maryam answers this question: ﴿She said, "It is from God"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37], then she mentions the reason for it: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37]. That is: beware of calculating matters by your own power, so that you say, "From where has summer fruit come to you in winter, or winter fruit in summer?" For this is the bounty of God and His power.

It was as though this statement from Lady Maryam alerted our master Zakariyya to a matter he had overlooked, and this word shook him: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37].

Then he said to himself: "Then why should I not supplicate God to grant me a son, after I have reached extreme old age and my wife is barren? The giving of God is not subject to causes." ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 38].

Thus our master Zakariyya benefited from this doctrinal matter that Lady Maryam had alerted him to, and God indeed responded to him and gave him a son, and He confirmed this even more by naming him for him: ﴿And the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed, God gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from God, and a noble leader, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 39].

This is a recording of the glad tidings and a confirmation of them. Among this is what is related of our master Abu Bakr: before he died, he advised Lady 'A'isha regarding the inheritance after him, saying to her: "Indeed, they are your two sisters and your two brothers." At the time she had only two brothers, namely 'Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad, and one sister, Lady Asma'. But after the death of the Siddiq, his wife Bint Kharija gave birth to a girl, and so the Siddiq's advice was confirmed. He, may God be pleased with him, did not have knowledge of the unseen; rather, he was taught it, and God made him speak of it, for none knows what is in the wombs except God. No one knows what is in the wombs by his own essence; rather, it is taught to him by God.

It is also related that our master, the Messenger of God, said to the people of Madina: he, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear that he would die in Madina, while God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman: 34].

So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know the unseen; rather, the unseen was taught to him by the All-Knowing of the unseen, glory be to Him. Therefore we do not say that so-and-so is a knower of the unseen; rather, he is one who is taught the unseen.

Thus we often see some of the righteous, or those from whom God has lifted the veil, look at a pregnant woman and say to her, "Name this child Muhammad," and indeed she gives birth to a child and names him Muhammad. This is a recording of glad tidings and an inspiration from God and a teaching to those whom God has chosen for this knowledge.

When people name their children, they choose the name by which they hope for good omen, saying: Sa'id, Dhaki, etc., hoping that the child will indeed be happy or intelligent. But can one control that the name will match what it names? No, no one can make his child as he wishes; but if the Namer is God, glory be to Him, then He alone is able to bring about what is named.

Therefore, when He granted our master Zakariyya a son and named him (Yahya), people did not perceive this naming, and that it was from God, meaning that this child would live and not die. God named him Yahya so that he would live. In this naming there is also an indication that he would die as a martyr, so the life of this world is joined to the life of martyrdom. Had his killers perceived this meaning, they would not have killed him.

Therefore, when we went to visit the grave of our master Hamza, we said there:

O Hamza, uncle of the Chosen One, you are a lord over all the martyrs of the earth, all of them;
and it suffices you of that martyrdom as a safeguard from death, in joining the two lives, this one to the next.

This doctrinal matter from which our master Zakariyya benefited, so that he asked God for a son, was later benefited from by Lady Maryam when she conceived without a male, so she remembered: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37], and her heart was reassured.

So the word (anna) in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how can they reach [such faith] from a far place?﴾ [Saba': 52], means "how," and similar to it is the saying of Lady Maryam when she was given the good tidings of 'Isa: ﴿How can I have a boy when no human has touched me?﴾ [Maryam: 20].

And like His saying: ﴿How will God bring this [town] to life after its death?﴾ [al-Baqara: 259], where the question here is about the manner of revival, a matter that is not told but is witnessed. Have we not read the saying of our master Ibrahim: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] that my heart may be at ease"﴾ [al-Baqara: 260].

The orientalists have an objection to this verse. They say: how does God address the father of the prophets, Ibrahim, saying to him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ [al-Baqara: 260], while he replies: ﴿Yes, but that my heart may be at ease﴾ [al-Baqara: 260], and is faith anything other than the heart's tranquillity in a certain belief?

We say: faith here differs from tranquillity. Faith that God gives life to the dead was already present in Ibrahim; he did not ask whether there is revival of the dead from God or not, since he believes in God's power to revive the dead. He asks about the manner of that, so the tranquillity intended is regarding the manner, as proof that God showed him a practical sign and a sensory experience in the matter of the slaughter of the birds, because the manner, as we said, is not stated by report but is witnessed.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, rejects the disbelievers' reaching for faith at this time: ﴿And how can they reach [such faith] from a far place?﴾ [Saba': 52]. Tanawush (reaching) is taking hold of a thing with ease. They want to take hold of faith at the last moment, after its time has passed and its opportunity is lost; they want faith without obligations, and how can that be for them, when they are furthest from faith, since the place of faith is the world. This statement of theirs is like the statement of their companions who said: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteousness other than what we used to do﴾ [Fatir: 37].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they had disbelieved in it before, and they hurl [assumptions] about the unseen...﴾

The meaning: He presented faith to them while they were in the comfort and ease of worldly life, and they rejected it. The world is the place of faith and the place of obligations, commands and prohibitions.
