So when they stood at the moment of death or resurrection, they wished for faith and said, "We believe," while they were in this state "casting at the unseen from a distant place" (yaqdhifūna bil-ghaybi min makānin baʿīd). That is, they speak by conjecture about what they have no knowledge of, wanting to reach their aim, which is to be saved from punishment. But this casting by conjecture also comes "from a distant place," meaning from something outside its proper place and time. Here the Qur'an attributed to them "qadhf" (casting), just as it attributed "qadhf" to the Truthful One, glorified is He: "Say: Indeed, my Lord casts with the truth" (Saba: 48). But there is a vast difference between the two.

The casting of these people is from a distant place, and casting from a distance does not hit the target. In their casting they do not know the unseen, nor do they know the influences that affect what is cast. As for the Truthful One, glorified is He, He casts, and He is the Knower of the unseen, from whose knowledge nothing is hidden.

We say: "Ḥultu bayna al-khaṣmayn" means: I separated the two adversaries, and I placed between them a barrier and a preventer against engaging one another, so that neither of them reaches his full strength in the battle, or attains his aim against his opponent. Thus Allah, glory be to Him, placed a barrier and a preventer between these people and what they desire.

Al-ishtihā' (desiring) is the pursuit of the soul's appetite without being bound by a method. But what was it that the disbelievers desired? They desired to extinguish the call to truth, but Allah did not enable them to extinguish it, as He said:

﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to complete His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 32].

And He said:

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it.﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 9].

They desired the obliteration of the call, so that their sovereignty, which they had seized at the expense of the weak, would remain, and so that they would continue to hold status and authority. Likewise they desired the obliteration of the call, so that the methods of Allah would not stand as an obstacle before the desires of their souls...

So His saying, ﴿and a barrier is placed between them and what they desire﴾ [Saba': 54], indicates that the matter, as far as they were concerned, was a desire of the soul, in which Satan had no part. Why? Because they had disbelieved in Allah, and Satan had finished with them. Otherwise, what would he want from them after that? Nothing remained but the desires of the soul, so they desired to extinguish the call, to humiliate whoever believed, and to make him an example for anyone who might think of believing. But Allah came between them and what they loved, and the call proceeded contrary to what they desired. Whoever among the believers was humiliated, struck, and disgraced remained steadfast in his faith, and whoever was considering faith was not terrified by them, nor frightened by what they did to his fellow believers.

If you ask: how did Allah let the early believers be subjected to torment by the disbelievers, to be humiliated and driven from their land? We say: this was for a lofty wisdom intended by the Truthful One, glory be to Him, namely that the faith of the believers be tested and purified, such that only those of firm resolve who endure the hardships would remain steadfast in their faith. These are the ones who would carry the methodology of heaven and the call to truth to the whole world, so they must be an elite who choose the religion of Allah and sacrifice for its sake everything precious and valuable.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, willed that this call be shaken at its beginning several times, and that some trials be seen which sift the people, bringing the believers to one side and the hypocrites to the other side...

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿as was done with their likes before﴾ [Saba': 54], meaning: this matter is not specific to the disbelievers of Makkah; rather it is a established sunnah among the earlier nations. The meaning of "bi-ashyā'ihim" is: with their counterparts among the disbelievers of the earlier nations.

Al-ashyā' is the plural of shī'ah, who are a group gathered around an opinion from which they benefit and which they defend, whether it is truth or falsehood. So His saying here: ﴿as was done with their likes before﴾ indicates that they were upon falsehood...

The meaning is: they were seized as their likes among the disbelievers were seized, with the difference between the two situations. Before the Messenger of Allah, heaven would intervene directly to defend the religion of Allah and the Prophet of Allah; therefore earthquakes, the sinking of the earth, the blast of the cry, and transformation into apes and swine occurred among them, etc.

The earlier nations were not trusted to defend the religion of Allah with their swords, whereas the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) was entrusted by Allah with this task. It bore the sword and defended its religion. Therefore Allah honored this nation, so no sinking, no transformation, and no drowning befell it, as happened to its predecessors.

Therefore, when Nuh (peace be upon him) despaired of the guidance of his people, he invoked against them:

﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a dweller. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers.﴾ [Nuh: 26-27].

As for our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the angel came to him offering to avenge him upon the disbelievers of his people, and he said: "No, perhaps Allah will bring forth from their loins those who say: there is no god but Allah." And indeed many of them believed, such as Khalid ibn al-Walid, 'Amr ibn al-'As, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and those who had been the fiercest enemies of Islam became its commanders and conquerors.

The Muslims greatly grieved because these people were spared from death, and they did not know that Allah, exalted is He, was reserving them for Islam. Khalid became the drawn sword of Allah, 'Amr became one of the greatest conquering commanders, and it suffices as testimony for 'Ikrimah that he was the son of Abu Jahl, and that when he was struck a severe blow at the battle of al-Yarmuk, Khalid embraced him while he was suffering the agonies of death, and he said: "O Khalid, is this a death that pleases Allah and His Messenger with me?"...

Then the surah concludes with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾ [Saba': 54]. They were in doubt about the matter of the Messenger of Allah, about his victory over them, and about his Lord not abandoning him, although they were in contact with the People of the Book, who read their scriptures to these disbelievers and sought victory through them against them. They knew from those scriptures that the outcome of the conflict between the messengers and their peoples throughout the course of prophethood was in favor of the messengers, because Allah, exalted is He, would not send a messenger and then hand him over or abandon him.

This is a matter mentioned in the previous scriptures, as it is mentioned in the Qur'an in more than one place. And although the previous scriptures were lost or distorted, the Qur'an is the enduring Book of Allah, whose preservation Allah has guaranteed. It is recited as it was revealed until the Day of Resurrection, and in it Allah, exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world.﴾ [Ghafir: 51].

And He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And已 Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they are the ones who will be given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers are they who will be the predominant.﴾ [al-Saffat: 171-173].

Therefore we have previously said: if Islam is defeated in a battle with another, know that the condition of faithful soldiership has been violated; and even if Allah granted them victory despite the violation of the condition of soldiership in them, no standing for Islam would be established after it. This lesson we learned at Uhud, when the archers disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and came down from the mountain seeking the spoils, although the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had warned them against this and said to them: "Do not leave your positions no matter what happens." When they left their positions, the disbelievers encircled them and nearly defeated them.

Yet the truth is that the disbelievers did not win at Uhud, because the battle [turned into a confused engagement] (ماعت); and if the Muslims had won despite this disobedience, the command of the Messenger would have seemed light to them afterward, and they would have said: "We disobeyed his command at Uhud and still won." So we say: whoever was defeated at Uhud was the one who withdrew from the soldiership of faith, while Islam in itself was victorious.

Thus: they were in doubt about the end toward which the Messenger of Allah was heading, and the doubt here was about the Messenger of Allah, because they had a doctrinal matter, namely belief in the existence of Allah, and that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of everything, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: Allah﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87].
